附录

尽管《Red Rooster》目前还没有可供玩家体验的版本，但在采访中，开发者也谈到了许多关于这款游戏的构想，包括它的视觉风格、世界设定、角色塑造和玩法设计。

我们认为，这些尚处于开发阶段的思考同样值得呈现，因此将相关问答作为额外内容放在采访最后，供读者参考。

游：说说游戏吧，你们是如何确定现在的视觉方向的？

Dora：从某种意义上来说，我们目前仍然处于探索阶段，希望尝试许多不同的风格。

我们邀请了十几位艺术家，让他们按照自己最自然、最习惯的风格去创作。因为我们想让同样的创意能够从不同角度得到呈现，并借此发现究竟有哪些东西能够真正打动我们。

我们喜欢左拉、斯坦贝克等20世纪作家的作品，关注现实中粗粝、不加修饰的部分，以及生活在特权阶层之外的普通人的处境。

我们希望将这种社会现实主义与迷幻、超现实的视觉元素结合起来。我后来开始把这类作品称为「心理角色扮演游戏（Psychological RPG）」——它们拥有一个带有社会现实主义色彩的外部世界，但玩法又有很大一部分发生在角色的内心世界中。

在《极乐迪斯科》中，这种表达体现在思维阁那些超现实的插画里。在我们的游戏中，我认为Laurie的迷幻艺术风格能让玩家感受到，这个世界不只有一个沉重压抑的外部环境，同时也存在着人类心智和感知本身所固有的奇异性。

游：我在书中看到一个很有意思的例子，你们参考了荷兰与比利时边境上的巴勒镇，两国领土在这里相互嵌套，国境线甚至会穿过街道、房屋和建筑内部。在游戏里，同一片街区可能分属不同国家，适用不同的法律和行政规定。你们曾提到，游戏世界融合了南斯拉夫、奥斯曼和荷兰文化，能说说你们这样选择的原因吗？

Dora：南斯拉夫的历史近来一直萦绕在我们脑海中，一方面是因为我们从英国搬到了这里，这片土地的历史也因此变得更加鲜明；另一方面，我和Aleks本来就来自这个地区，这里也是我们的故乡。

但即使我曾经去过世界上很多地方，巴尔干地区给我留下的印象依然很深。它是不同文化圈的交汇点，西欧、东欧和中东在这里相遇。历史上，这里一直是不同势力和文化发生碰撞的地方，包括奥斯曼帝国、奥匈帝国以及斯拉夫文化。

我们通常熟悉的是两种文化之间的边界，而三种文化交汇形成的边界则是完全不同的存在。这也是为什么有一种说法：巴尔干家庭的每一代人都经历过一场战争，下一代也总会经历战争。

尽管这种环境往往充满动荡，但它在文化上也非常有意思。比如波斯尼亚这样的地方，不同宗教和不同风格的建筑可以并存。巴尔干地区实际上非常适合作为一个幻想世界的基础，我们可以从现实生活中汲取大量灵感。

在游戏里，同一片街区可能分属不同国家，适用不同的法律和行政规定。比如，酒类销售时间一到，酒吧里的顾客就得从一个国家的区域搬到另一个国家；政治关系发生变化后，原本可以直接穿越的边境也可能被封锁，玩家不得不寻找穿过小巷、公园甚至窗户的新路线。

游：游戏的主角Redrick是一个缺乏内在自主性的人，他还有一位有着强迫性说谎倾向的伙伴Astrid。你们是如何设计这两个角色的？

Dora：我们希望摆脱一些刻板印象。对于Redrick，我们不想塑造一个非常阳刚、能够满足玩家力量幻想的主角。Redrick在人生中一直更多地被他人推动着前进，可能从未真正坚定地表达过自己的意愿，也缺乏足够的自信。我们希望玩家从这样的状态开始，再决定要把他带向哪里，以及他最终能够走到什么地方。

Astrid则是他的反面。我们想让她成为一位数学家，帮助Redrick解开世界的谜团。她在生活中拥有很强的自主性，但她并不会利用这种自主性来安排和掌控事情的发展。这种特点也会体现在玩法中，比如她会自主采取行动，影响游戏环境。

我们希望借此打破RPG中常见的同伴关系。传统游戏里的同伴通常随时听候玩家调遣，像工具一样提供帮助。但Astrid并不总能正常发挥作用，也不一定会公平地对待你，也可能误导玩家或犯下严重错误。玩家需要思考如何与她相处，并决定两人最终建立怎样的关系。

Laurie：我希望角色首先呈现出自己的个性，而不是外貌有多符合审美标准。很多电子游戏，尤其是RPG，喜欢塑造理想化的主角形象。我更希望他们扎根于现实，有粗粝、缺陷和不完美之处，看起来像我们生活中真正可能遇到的人。

Redrick身上有一种孩子气，也带着某种天真，仿佛他做什么都没有恶意。他的眉毛向上弯曲，让他看起来有些天真无邪。此外，他的胡子也是角色身份的重要标志，我觉得可以拿Harry那条令人印象深刻的领带和他的络腮胡作类比。

Astrid也是一个很复杂的人物。我希望Astrid有现实中的粗粝感，同时又有一种满不在乎的很酷的气质。她有比较突出的鼻子，以及蓬乱的头发，甚至有点像《指环王》里的咕噜。编剧还特别强调，不要把她设计得太漂亮，宁可让她显得年纪大一些，也不要刻意把她画年轻。

我的工作就是理解编剧对人物的构想，再通过视觉设计呈现出来。我们希望塑造的角色有丰富的内在，让玩家能够在他们身上看到自己，或者现实中认识的人。Harry和Kim就是很好的例子，他们并不符合传统电子游戏主角的外貌标准，但玩家了解他们之后，仍然会对他们产生深厚的感情。

游：我记得你们采访Mark Darrah时，他谈到过游戏开发中的一个常见问题，玩法系统与叙事意图经常显得彼此脱节。你怎么看待玩法与叙事之间长期存在的这种割裂？在《Red Rooster》的开发中，你们打算如何处理这个问题？

Dora：这种脱节往往源于游戏类型过早确定，而类型选择通常受到商业和市场营销的影响。比如，团队决定制作一款第一人称射击游戏，就意味着必须包含相应的战斗机制。玩法框架先于故事确定，之后才开始考虑叙事。

这也容易造成玩法与人物塑造之间的矛盾。比如，过场动画里的Nathan Drake是一个有血有肉的人物，到了实际游戏中却可以杀掉一百五十个人。

另一种做法是从核心创意和故事出发，再决定需要什么样的机制来强化它。《极乐迪斯科》就是一个例子。这类创新更多出现在独立游戏和2A游戏中，因为3A游戏往往受到市场需求和玩家预期的限制。

如果开发者拥有更多时间和财务上的自由，就能尝试自己真正想做的东西，也更有机会创造新的玩法和游戏类型。

游：我记得Mark Darrah也提出过，叙事应该先于机制，但开发叙事可能需要很长时间。你们如何协调叙事开发与制作流程中其他部分的进度？

Dora：这确实涉及制作流程上的取舍。我们目前采取的方式是并行开发叙事和一个小型可玩Demo。我们先搭建一块区域，测试物理交互，比如物体和火焰的运作方式，以及玩家在空间中的移动体验。与此同时，团队也在确定故事、世界观和角色。

这种方式可能导致两条开发线暂时脱节，但也让我们能够快速验证设计方案，舍弃不合适的玩法。

真正容易出现问题的是管理层急于推进流程，要求团队过早敲定设计，或者强迫编剧和玩法开发保持相同的进度。

我认同Mark Darrah所说的，以写作为主导的工作室，确实需要警惕在叙事上投入过多时间。但我们决定成为这样的工作室，也愿意接受它带来的效率损失。

行业里已经有很多工作室会优先开发玩法，或者更加侧重玩法设计。我们不认为所有团队都应该采用我们的方式，甚至不是所有人都会享受我们这种工作方式。但我们确实喜欢这样做，因为我们的编剧实在太多了。

游：我记得Argo在书中把「物理性」上升到存在论层面，称这是角色扮演最纯粹的形式。「物理性」为什么会如此重要？

Argo：我认为这要回到小时候的游戏经验。孩子最初通过身体模仿周围的世界，比如把圆环套在方块上，模拟战斗，或者模仿去街角商店购物。随着年龄增长，游戏逐渐变得复杂，但这些具体的行动始终很重要。

在游戏中，玩家伸手拿起一件东西、把它搬到别处，或者打开一扇门，这些看似简单的行为，都会在潜意识层面强化玩家与角色、角色与世界之间的联系。

游：这听起来有些类似沙盒游戏？

Argo：老实说，我认为两者之间真正的区别可能只在于复杂程度。可以说，我们做的是一种轻量化的沙盒游戏，我们需要处理的复杂程度稍低一些。

像《Deus Ex》这样的沉浸式模拟游戏，包含大量战斗和潜行机制，会产生许多需要处理的变量。移除这些系统后，设计的复杂程度就相对容易控制，但依然是一项很大的挑战。

游：我记得你在文章中称环境本身是一个重要的「非玩家角色」，也认为这是一种重新思考和拓展传统RPG环境设计方式的途径。能否具体解释一下游戏中的「动态街区」（Dynamic District）是如何运作的？

Argo：它是由几套不同的事件卡组组合而成的。游戏中每天都会定期抽取随机事件，同时也会发生一些预先编排好的事件。

这些事件的规模差异很大，有些是非常重大的事件，比如你所在街区的一栋房子突然烧毁。规模较小的事件则更接近环境叙事，如果你留意周围的环境，就会发现一些细小的视觉故事在多个游戏日之间逐渐展开。

传统游戏往往通过让玩家从起始区域前往新的区域来推进进程，也就是不断在空间上向前移动。而这个小型开放世界允许我们在时间维度上推进。游戏世界中的每一天，玩家都会重新看到这个熟悉的街区。因为你已经熟悉了原本的状态，各种细微的变化就会格外显眼，并立刻引起你的好奇。

对我来说，这种环境随机性的设计思路来自桌游。游戏进行到某个阶段，就会触发某种随机事件，而且，玩家此前做出的选择会改变之后抽取的事件卡组。有时你甚至不知道究竟有多少种可能，因为你只知道自己尚不了解的那些内容。即使你不知道卡组里到底有多少张牌，你的想象通常也会认为实际可能性比真实情况更多。

游：你们如何避免玩家太快摸清事件池的规律，或者觉得这些事件开始变得重复？

Argo：这种情况会发生吗？从系统设计之初，我们就确保玩家在一次完整的游戏流程中不可能看到所有事件。有些事件本身就是互斥的，无法在同一轮游戏中同时出现。此外，事件的总数量也超过了游戏实际包含的天数。

游：Andrus在文章中谈到了庄子、禅宗和爵士乐，还把音频设计师的工作描述为在一片根本不存在针的干草堆里寻找一根针。这些想法听起来都相当抽象，也很有哲学意味。它们在实际创作中是如何体现的？能否结合《极乐迪斯科》或《Red Rooster》举一些具体例子？

Andrus：游戏核心理念中已经存在的某种结构，只要你从这个起点出发，什么东西都可以拿来使用。

我可以从早期的一次创作经历讲起。当时我们为一部爱沙尼亚导演执导的戏剧配乐，最后一幕是人们开始跳舞。我考虑使用爱尔兰传统音乐，但又犹豫了很久。虽然导演是爱尔兰人，但这一幕与爱尔兰文化并没有直接联系，而音乐本身又承载着很强的文化背景。

我一开始想的是我不能用，但突然就像一道闪光打在我身上，我明白了，其实我可以在任何地方用任何东西。你只需要找到方法。你可以从音乐的动态、结构等方面入手，减弱它原有的文化语境，让它成为对场景本身的声音表达。

你必须感受到场景与声音或音乐之间存在一种身体层面的联系。如果你感受不到这种联系，就必须继续寻找。你要一直寻找，直到听到那个瞬间的契合，直到声音与场景之间产生一种身体层面的正确感。

这是一种非常个人化、因人而异的工作方式。至少到目前为止，它一直有效。我希望它在《Red Rooster》接下来的创作过程中也能继续发挥作用。

title: 团队规模30+，广州居然还藏了一家IAA游戏大佬
text:
团队规模30+，广州居然还藏了一家IAA游戏大佬
游戏新知君
2026-11-19 18:15 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
作者 | 鳗鱼
广深游戏圈藏了一批主攻IAA小游戏的厂商，其中广州尊悦游戏大概就是相对低调的一家。
去年尊悦游戏旗下的小游戏《打个螺丝》就曾因为在朋友圈引发大量用户的跟风评论而破圈，游戏使用的「别笑，你来你也过不了第二关」文案也给许多玩家留下了深刻印象，而尊悦游戏也因此开始受到关注。
有些令人意外的是，明明这套广告词谁都能用，但似乎只有尊悦游戏才耍得最为有效，几乎说是品牌标识也不为过。
比方说最近涌现了一批整理房间题材的消除游戏，包括广州尊悦、长沙指色、厦门营火、武汉多比特等深耕小游戏的厂商都有新品挤进微信小游戏畅玩榜。而尊悦游戏的两款游戏《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》就沿用了之前的标志性文案，甚至都不用点进游戏里就能知道是尊悦游戏的新品。
凭借着出众的敏感度和发行经验，尊悦游戏又一次抢到了品类热度，这家成立不过几年的游戏公司似乎也已经藏不住了。
又追上了热门玩法
《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》都属于堆叠消除类的玩法，对于现在的尊悦游戏来说正是熟悉的类型。而且两款游戏都同时冲进微信小游戏畅玩榜TOP20，《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》分别排在第2名和第15名。
来源：引力引擎
玩家在游戏中需要根据物品类型进行收纳，比如衣物、电子产品、乐器、文具等，在收纳指定数量的物品后，相应的收纳箱会自动进行打包。房间中的物品相互堆叠摆放，玩家必须先收纳上层的物品，才能进而与下层的物品交互。
游戏也提供了临时储放区，以供玩家收纳下一层的物品。当临时储放区超过上限后，游戏便视为闯关失败。在同一关卡中，相同类型的收纳箱可能会重复出现。玩家需要仔细观察物品的分布再进行收纳，如果能够优先收纳处于重叠状态的物品，那么就可以变相节省临时储放区的位置。
所以相比起以往的堆叠消除游戏，采用收纳题材之后也造就了一种新的玩法类型。
堆叠消除玩法至今已经出现了许多种类，比如卡牌形式的《Zen Match》、3D物品类型的《Match Factory!》等，在国内市场也陆续出现了《羊了个羊》《抓大鹅》等现象级产品。包括尊悦游戏的爆款《打个螺丝》也可以算在堆叠消除的类型中。
而《疯狂收杂物》这类显然结合了侦探寻物的玩法体验。除了「按顺序消除」之外，「寻物」也是玩法的一大难点。游戏中的物品都以不规则的形状摆放，而且根据种类的不同，物品大小也有着明显的区别。比如长裤、帽子、乐器、书籍等大件物品就更容易识别，而短裤和短裙等一般物品在堆叠状态下有可能被混淆，纸团、易拉罐、钥匙等小件物品则不太容易被识别。
在游戏过程中，玩家有时候会遇到明明可以看见，但因为观察不仔细而漏掉的情况。或者有可能在连续收纳了大件物品之后，因为露出了底下的小物品而跳出死局。
为此，游戏的玩法设计也做出了相应的优化。玩家可以双指放大游戏画面，以便寻找较小的物品。另外在关卡前期中，如果玩家有一段时间没有操作，游戏也会高亮显示出目标物品作为提示。
针对新的玩法类型，游戏在运营设计方面同样作出了新调整。玩家观看广告除了可以获得额外的收纳箱之外，还可以获得额外的临时储放区，甚至无视障碍物直接装满指定的收纳箱。这不仅显著降低了玩法难度，也为游戏提供了新的广告变现入口。
另外《疯狂收杂物》的难度设计也体现了尊悦游戏的经验积累。
区别于最早《羊了个羊》火遍全网的时候，当时「你试你也过不了第二关」属于名副其实，而《疯狂收杂物》虽然也会随着关卡的推进而扩大场景规格、增加物品数量，但实际的难度曲线更为平滑，往往到第三关之后才感受到难度提升。类似的调整其实在《打个螺丝》身上就有所应用。结合朋友圈的广告栏位，有的用户就会在在广告下评论表示自己「过了」，也更容易勾起其他好友的兴趣和好奇心。
在买量投放方面，《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》形成了错位，这也得以让两款游戏都能同时冲上微信小游戏人气榜。
DataEye的数据显示，两款游戏的投放素材量级相近，投放文案也都同样使用了「把房间收拾好！」「不会有人这关都过不去吧」，着重表现收拾房间的题材亮点。不同的是《疯狂收杂物》侧重使用视频素材，在微信主投小程序激励广告；而《益智闯一关》则侧重使用图片素材，主投朋友圈广告。
《疯狂收杂物》的视频素材中多数在直接展示或解说游戏本身的玩法，比如介绍物品堆叠、临时储放等一系列玩法规则。部分素材则通过现实中的收纳经验过渡到游戏的玩法技巧，引导玩家优先收纳纸箱等大件物品，再依次收纳衣架、电脑配件等。
《益智闯一关》的图片素材则主要展示了收纳前的房间，除此之外还关联了一些其他堆叠消除、或者是类似寻物的玩法画面。其共同点是画面内容都呈现出密集分布的特点，和本身的游戏内容有着相似的观感。
目前这类收纳题材的消除游戏在海外刚刚开始受到关注，而在国内已经迅速成为了IAA游戏共同追逐的热点。类似于ASMR清洁题材，收纳题材同样也是解压治愈的一个分支，在社交媒体平台上的相应内容也都有不错的热度，这也给新玩法带来了一定数量的潜在受众。
尊悦游戏虽然不是唯一一家抓住这类题材的厂商，但凭借着对消除玩法的嗅觉迅速跟上了热点，也再一次加深了玩家对于「你试你也过不了第二关」这句广告词和尊悦游戏的关联。
一句广告词，什么玩法都能套
现在尊悦游戏已经决心瞄准消除品类，而这也是这句广告词能够被反反复复利用的原因之一。
综合公开信息得知，尊悦游戏在2021年底成立，早期发行过成语、找茬、消除等不同类型的产品，包括《拼词达人秀》《爆笑找茬》《抢滩对战》《药水勇者》等。2024年公司开始转型聚焦于中度消除品类，团队规模也逐步扩张到2025年的10多人、今年的30多人。
第一款走红的招牌产品自然就是2024年的《打个螺丝》。当时公司日消耗峰值破300万，很大程度上也是得益于这款产品。
《打个螺丝》在2024年8月上线，上线早期其实就已经闯入过微信小游戏平台的TOP10，半年后排名稍有下滑，但仍保持在TOP40。后来官方披露的数据显示，游戏次留达到10%、90日留存达到1%。
2025年上半年，尊悦游戏再次发行了同类的拧螺丝产品《折螺丝》和《疯狂玩螺丝》。其中《折螺丝》因为朋友圈广告引发的热潮而出圈，不过真正导入吸量的依然是老产品《打个螺丝》，同年5月冲上了畅玩榜榜首，过去一年多里也保持在TOP20。尽管《疯狂玩螺丝》不及《打个螺丝》火爆，但同样在坚持在畅玩榜TOP100的中下游。
而且朋友圈广告还具有一定的长尾效应。直到现在仍可以看到《打个螺丝》广告投放，通过评论区内容可以看出来这是2025年以来积累的互动内容。此前尊悦游戏的商务清瑶也曾在微信官方的播客中回应了「被盗号评论」的说法，其解释表示广告会将投放周期内的评论汇聚在一起重复曝光，所以一条广告就会积累数月甚至上年的互动内容。
靠着《打个螺丝》这个爆款，尊悦游戏做到了微信小游戏平台上少有的长线。并且对比《疯狂来解压》等同类产品，现在已经几乎在微信小游戏平台上独自吃下了拧螺丝这一玩法品类。
「第二关」的广告文案也吸引了其他产品的跟进，比如《解压螺丝》《全民打螺丝》等，但基本都没达到《打个螺丝》的效果。与此同时，尊悦游戏也将这句广告词套在了其他的消除玩法类型上，比如《Food Hunt》的《消除玩个够》。
另外表现比较出彩的还有水果消除类产品。今年尊悦游戏接连推出了《消个水果》《消个水果游戏》《躺平消除》，前两者都曾闯入微信小游戏畅玩榜TOP10，而《躺平消除》也最高闯到TOP40。
《消个水果》《消个水果游戏》同样延续了「第二关」的广告文案，官方还在今年透露《消个水果》次留达到了12%、90日留存达到1.6%，成功复用了之前的发行模式。后续游戏排名都有所下滑，但《消个水果》和《消个水果游戏》在同题材玩法的赛道中也依然是头部产品。
尽管尊悦游戏没有能够复现《打个螺丝》身上的朋友圈广告热潮，但依然在不同消除玩法中继续沿用「第二关」的广告文案，而且也确实接连做出了爆款。
抛开包袱做新尝试
现在尊悦游戏靠着朋友圈广告一战成名，但也并非彻底咬着这套发行方案不放。
比如通过旗下的倒水排序游戏《倒水杯》就能看出尊悦游戏在推广打法上的变通。去年《打个螺丝》和「第二关」广告文案爆火了之后，尊悦游戏便上线了新品《倒水杯》，游戏很快也冲上了微信小游戏畅玩榜TOP20。今年初游戏排名随之投放的减少而出现了大幅下滑，但近半年来又通过小幅起量在逐渐回暖到畅玩榜30多名。
而《倒水杯》在尊悦游戏的产品矩阵中显得格外特殊，原因就在于游戏没有在简介中套用「第二关」的文案，看起来反而比较普通。
从推广素材来看，早期《倒水杯》其实也用了不少「第二关」的广告文案。而在今年表现回暖之前，相关的推广素材则是直接在图片中附带了「第二关」的文案，而配文则是「我要开始倒水了！」「这真的不能算我菜吧」等。即便使用相对常规的推广打法，尊悦游戏似乎也同样能够做出爆款来。
此外，朋友圈广告的打法虽然只能在微信奏效，但微信小游戏平台也不是唯一选择。
尊悦游戏的发行主体虽然专注于微信小游戏平台，但另一个疑似关联的公司主体广州尚游文化也在抖音小游戏平台上同步了多款产品，只不过至今都还没有特别出彩的表现。
另外值得关注的是，去年广州尚游文化还成立了一家子公司广州尊悦创界信息，并且由武汉当看持有30%的股权。武汉当看则是武汉多比特的关联公司，后者的代表产品包括《Cell Survivor》《Blossom Sort》《猫咪寻物记》《Car Jam》等，某种程度上也代表着尊悦游戏已经打出了名声。
包括在今年，尊悦游戏的关联公司主体的广州乐逍遥还参股了一家新的公司广州尊悦星澜文化。该公司主体由另一家初创公司深圳沐游方舟持有80%股份、乐逍遥则持有20%，猜测也是为后续的产品合作做准备。
尊悦游戏自从聚焦消除品类之后，现在已经形成了一套心得和方法论，也展示了连续推出爆款的能力。而且尊悦游戏也不满足手头的发行套路，在现有的发行经验基础上，说不定还会进而关注起其他市场的机会。
结语
近两年来尊悦游戏成功在市场竞争中抓到了空档，找准方向后俨然成为了IAA赛道上的一支新锐。在去年的小游戏百强榜上，尊悦游戏在广州IAA小游戏厂商已经仅次于广州指上科技，而在今年继续推出爆款之后，预计竞争力也将进一步上升。

团队规模30+，广州居然还藏了一家IAA游戏大佬

游戏新知君

2026-11-19 18:15发布于湖北游戏新知官方账号

关注

作者 | 鳗鱼


广深游戏圈藏了一批主攻IAA小游戏的厂商，其中广州尊悦游戏大概就是相对低调的一家。


去年尊悦游戏旗下的小游戏《打个螺丝》就曾因为在朋友圈引发大量用户的跟风评论而破圈，游戏使用的「别笑，你来你也过不了第二关」文案也给许多玩家留下了深刻印象，而尊悦游戏也因此开始受到关注。


有些令人意外的是，明明这套广告词谁都能用，但似乎只有尊悦游戏才耍得最为有效，几乎说是品牌标识也不为过。


比方说最近涌现了一批整理房间题材的消除游戏，包括广州尊悦、长沙指色、厦门营火、武汉多比特等深耕小游戏的厂商都有新品挤进微信小游戏畅玩榜。而尊悦游戏的两款游戏《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》就沿用了之前的标志性文案，甚至都不用点进游戏里就能知道是尊悦游戏的新品。



凭借着出众的敏感度和发行经验，尊悦游戏又一次抢到了品类热度，这家成立不过几年的游戏公司似乎也已经藏不住了。




又追上了热门玩法


《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》都属于堆叠消除类的玩法，对于现在的尊悦游戏来说正是熟悉的类型。而且两款游戏都同时冲进微信小游戏畅玩榜TOP20，《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》分别排在第2名和第15名。


来源：引力引擎


玩家在游戏中需要根据物品类型进行收纳，比如衣物、电子产品、乐器、文具等，在收纳指定数量的物品后，相应的收纳箱会自动进行打包。房间中的物品相互堆叠摆放，玩家必须先收纳上层的物品，才能进而与下层的物品交互。


游戏也提供了临时储放区，以供玩家收纳下一层的物品。当临时储放区超过上限后，游戏便视为闯关失败。在同一关卡中，相同类型的收纳箱可能会重复出现。玩家需要仔细观察物品的分布再进行收纳，如果能够优先收纳处于重叠状态的物品，那么就可以变相节省临时储放区的位置。



所以相比起以往的堆叠消除游戏，采用收纳题材之后也造就了一种新的玩法类型。


堆叠消除玩法至今已经出现了许多种类，比如卡牌形式的《Zen Match》、3D物品类型的《Match Factory!》等，在国内市场也陆续出现了《羊了个羊》《抓大鹅》等现象级产品。包括尊悦游戏的爆款《打个螺丝》也可以算在堆叠消除的类型中。


而《疯狂收杂物》这类显然结合了侦探寻物的玩法体验。除了「按顺序消除」之外，「寻物」也是玩法的一大难点。游戏中的物品都以不规则的形状摆放，而且根据种类的不同，物品大小也有着明显的区别。比如长裤、帽子、乐器、书籍等大件物品就更容易识别，而短裤和短裙等一般物品在堆叠状态下有可能被混淆，纸团、易拉罐、钥匙等小件物品则不太容易被识别。


在游戏过程中，玩家有时候会遇到明明可以看见，但因为观察不仔细而漏掉的情况。或者有可能在连续收纳了大件物品之后，因为露出了底下的小物品而跳出死局。


为此，游戏的玩法设计也做出了相应的优化。玩家可以双指放大游戏画面，以便寻找较小的物品。另外在关卡前期中，如果玩家有一段时间没有操作，游戏也会高亮显示出目标物品作为提示。



针对新的玩法类型，游戏在运营设计方面同样作出了新调整。玩家观看广告除了可以获得额外的收纳箱之外，还可以获得额外的临时储放区，甚至无视障碍物直接装满指定的收纳箱。这不仅显著降低了玩法难度，也为游戏提供了新的广告变现入口。


另外《疯狂收杂物》的难度设计也体现了尊悦游戏的经验积累。


区别于最早《羊了个羊》火遍全网的时候，当时「你试你也过不了第二关」属于名副其实，而《疯狂收杂物》虽然也会随着关卡的推进而扩大场景规格、增加物品数量，但实际的难度曲线更为平滑，往往到第三关之后才感受到难度提升。类似的调整其实在《打个螺丝》身上就有所应用。结合朋友圈的广告栏位，有的用户就会在在广告下评论表示自己「过了」，也更容易勾起其他好友的兴趣和好奇心。


在买量投放方面，《疯狂收杂物》和《益智闯一关》形成了错位，这也得以让两款游戏都能同时冲上微信小游戏人气榜。


DataEye的数据显示，两款游戏的投放素材量级相近，投放文案也都同样使用了「把房间收拾好！」「不会有人这关都过不去吧」，着重表现收拾房间的题材亮点。不同的是《疯狂收杂物》侧重使用视频素材，在微信主投小程序激励广告；而《益智闯一关》则侧重使用图片素材，主投朋友圈广告。



《疯狂收杂物》的视频素材中多数在直接展示或解说游戏本身的玩法，比如介绍物品堆叠、临时储放等一系列玩法规则。部分素材则通过现实中的收纳经验过渡到游戏的玩法技巧，引导玩家优先收纳纸箱等大件物品，再依次收纳衣架、电脑配件等。


《益智闯一关》的图片素材则主要展示了收纳前的房间，除此之外还关联了一些其他堆叠消除、或者是类似寻物的玩法画面。其共同点是画面内容都呈现出密集分布的特点，和本身的游戏内容有着相似的观感。


目前这类收纳题材的消除游戏在海外刚刚开始受到关注，而在国内已经迅速成为了IAA游戏共同追逐的热点。类似于ASMR清洁题材，收纳题材同样也是解压治愈的一个分支，在社交媒体平台上的相应内容也都有不错的热度，这也给新玩法带来了一定数量的潜在受众。



尊悦游戏虽然不是唯一一家抓住这类题材的厂商，但凭借着对消除玩法的嗅觉迅速跟上了热点，也再一次加深了玩家对于「你试你也过不了第二关」这句广告词和尊悦游戏的关联。

此外，朋友圈广告的打法虽然只能在微信奏效，但微信小游戏平台也不是唯一选择。


尊悦游戏的发行主体虽然专注于微信小游戏平台，但另一个疑似关联的公司主体广州尚游文化也在抖音小游戏平台上同步了多款产品，只不过至今都还没有特别出彩的表现。


另外值得关注的是，去年广州尚游文化还成立了一家子公司广州尊悦创界信息，并且由武汉当看持有30%的股权。武汉当看则是武汉多比特的关联公司，后者的代表产品包括《Cell Survivor》《Blossom Sort》《猫咪寻物记》《Car Jam》等，某种程度上也代表着尊悦游戏已经打出了名声。



包括在今年，尊悦游戏的关联公司主体的广州乐逍遥还参股了一家新的公司广州尊悦星澜文化。该公司主体由另一家初创公司深圳沐游方舟持有80%股份、乐逍遥则持有20%，猜测也是为后续的产品合作做准备。


尊悦游戏自从聚焦消除品类之后，现在已经形成了一套心得和方法论，也展示了连续推出爆款的能力。而且尊悦游戏也不满足手头的发行套路，在现有的发行经验基础上，说不定还会进而关注起其他市场的机会。



结语


近两年来尊悦游戏成功在市场竞争中抓到了空档，找准方向后俨然成为了IAA赛道上的一支新锐。在去年的小游戏百强榜上，尊悦游戏在广州IAA小游戏厂商已经仅次于广州指上科技，而在今年继续推出爆款之后，预计竞争力也将进一步上升。

title: 18 unsolicited third-party statistics about GTA 6
author: Jon Hicks
excerpt:
Officially, GTA 6 releases on Thursday, the 19th November. In practice, the first players in New Zealand, or claiming to be in New Zealand , fired it up on the 18th in the UK and US, and dozens of reviews have been published worldwide . Mainstream media coverage has been running all day, and will continue into the morning as the game goes on sale. In response to this highly anticipated global event, marketeers across the globe have deluged the world's media with uncertain claims of product relevancy.

text:
Officially, GTA 6 releases on Thursday, the 19th November. In practice, the first players in New Zealand, or claiming to be in New Zealand , fired it up on the 18th in the UK and US, and dozens of reviews have been published worldwide . Mainstream media coverage has been running all day, and will continue into the morning as the game goes on sale. In response to this highly anticipated global event, marketeers across the globe have deluged the world's media with uncertain claims of product relevancy.
Our inbox has filled with opportunistic press releases attempting to catch a sliver of the game's huge cultural impact, and direct it to everything from mattresses to car tyres to domestic help. Some of them are seeking to get their client coverage, others are trying for the SEO benefit of links from a media outlet. Most of them have offered expert comment, and many of them have offered data, invariably based on surveys conducted specifically to support their pitch.
We don't have time to write up all these pitches, and it's doubtful that most of them would be relevant to you anyway. The games industry is well-informed on the impact of Grand Theft Auto, as demonstrated by the number of releases that have fled its arrival . But there's a lot of data in there, and perhaps you need something to drop into a presentation, so we have collected some highlights.
Almost a third (30%) of players who work from home said they may use working hours to play the new game. (Uswitch)
8% of US adult gamers will take holiday or adjust their work schedule to play the game (PCMag)
887,515 UK workers may take sick leave to play the game (Uswitch)
46% of GTA 6 players have graduated from school since the previous GTA game released (Unwind Media)
47% of Gen Z survey respondents "report being excited about the upcoming release" (Ipsos)
36% of them are worried about missing out on conversations if they don't play it
16% intend to wake up earlier than usual to squeeze in extra gaming time (MattressNextDay)
12% of UK players saw the gameplay leaks over the summer (YouGov)
Of those, 46% said that seeing the leaked footage made them more excited about the game, and 4% said it made them less excited
1% of players said that $100 for the Ultimate Edition of the game was too cheap (firstlook.gg)
37% of players would prefer to purchase a major release like GTA on a physical disc (G2A)
38% preferred digital
There was a 25% increase in total data downloaded on the day that the preload started (GigaClear)
The download volume peaked at 1.2 terabytes per second (CityFibre)
Retail purchases of Take-Two Interactive stock have increased 150% WoW (Freetrade)
GTA 6 has been the most-wanted game in Nielsen's weekly ratings for over 150 weeks (Nielsen)
Annual leave bookings for the 19th in the UK are 40% higher than would otherwise be expected (Timetastic)
22% of gamers are prepared to cut back on takeways to afford a new console to play GTA 6, and 13% would buy cheaper Christmas presents (Virgin Media O2).
Use this information as you will. We will report the game's performance figures as soon as we receive them; given Sensor Tower's projection of $1.4B in pre-order revenue , and Take Two CEO Strauss Zelnick's prior description of the pre-order volumes as " unprecedented ", it seems likely we'll have sales figures before the week is out.

title: Arknights: Endfield named Google Play's best game of 2026
author: Vikki Blake
excerpt:
Gryphline's Arknights: Endfield has been named Google Play's best game of 2026, taking the top prize in every market except Japan and Korea.
Read more
text:
Gryphline's Arknights: Endfield has been named Google Play's best game of 2026, taking the top prize in every market except Japan and Korea.
Google announced the winners on November 17 in a blog post from Sam Bright, VP and general manager of Google Play and its developer ecosystem. Hololive Dreams won best game in Japan, while Nexon's MapleStory: Idle RPG won in Korea.
Bright said this year's picks reflected a shift toward games that span phones, tablets, and PCs, and highlighted Arknights: Endfield's Sidekick integration and its cross-device play through Google Play Games on PC.
XSeed Games' farming sim Moonlight Peaks won best cross-device game in the main list. Perfect World's Neverness to Everness took the same award in many Asian markets.
Digital Extremes' Warframe was named best multiplayer game and Sybo's Subway Surfers City won best pick up and play. Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor, published by Ghost Ship Publishing, won best indie, and Sea of Stars, published by Playdigious on mobile, won best story. Hoyoverse's Zenless Zone Zero won best ongoing game in the Americas and Europe.
Outside games, note-taking app Notability was named best app, and Strava won best cross-device app. Google's Asia Pacific list also included regional awards, with Blast+ Games' Scarfall 2.0 named best made in India and Own Games' Tukang Sate VS Ojol Rush best made in Indonesia.
Arknights: Endfield is also a finalist for iPad Game of the Year in Apple's App Store Awards 2026 , revealed earlier today, and is nominated for best mobile game at The Game Awards alongside Monster Hunter Outlanders, Neverness to Everness, Pokémon Champions, and Where Winds Meet. Winners will be revealed on December 10.
Last month, Google Play added a batch of new discovery and social features for games , including a personalized Game Finder, timed competitive Sprints, and clip-sharing via its Sidekick overlay.

title: Rockstar and IWGB members issue closing arguments following conclusion of employment tribunal
author: Sophie McEvoy
excerpt:
The employment tribunal between Rockstar and members of the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB) has concluded, with both parties issuing their closing arguments.
Read more
text:
The employment tribunal between Rockstar and members of the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB) has concluded, with both parties issuing their closing arguments.
The tribunal concerned the dismissal of 34 employees last year. Rockstar alleged they "distributed and discussed confidential information in a public forum, breaching company policy and their legal obligations."
The claimants, including 23 of the affected employees, argued they were dismissed for union activities. Richard O'Keeffe and Lord John Hendy KC represented them at the tribunal.
As reported by BBC News , O'Keeffe stated that Rockstar management was aware of the Discord server for three years but took no action until union membership neared 10%.
"As grim as it is to see and to have to recognise, these posts simply were not the respondents' reason, far less their principal reason for dismissal," said O'Keeffe.
"Those respondent witnesses I've mentioned simply did not regard IWGB as a good fit for them, by which we can infer they meant too confrontational, too effective, and wished to prevent them gaining any leverage or power over the respondent."
Additional reporting from Sky News included further comment from O'Keeffe about the nature of the Discord server. "Those union members and organising committee members made extensive use of a private online forum for their activities, the server."
"Despite those individuals' extensive knowledge of the server, the nature of the discussions of working conditions, the criticism that management received and the presence of IWGB officials and, inadvertently, a number of ex-employees, no action was taken to investigate or raise any disciplinary concern about the server over three years until October 7 [2025], when one of their covert informants relayed that IWGB was approaching 10% member density within the workforce."
O'Keeffe referred to comments by HR executive Charlie Kinloch, noting that by October 2025, the server had grown to include 10 ex-employees, compared to three when it started. "If disparagement and sharing of HR communications in a server of 350 people and 10 ex-employees was genuinely viewed as gross misconduct, it would be similarly concerning in a server of 250 people and three ex-employees."
"That disparagement and discussion of HR communications was not viewed as gross misconduct; it wasn't concerning."
Rockstar was represented by Thomas Cordrey. In his closing statement , he said the server's moderators did not want to "over police" the platform and "let the taps of disparagement and confidential information flow," which he alleged included release timings for GTA 6 and unreleased features.
"This was a case of 'we know the policies, we know our employer would be opposed to the use of a semi-public Discord to disparage and breach confidentiality, but we did it anyway and we would do it again," said Cordrey.
"The reason why these individuals were dismissed was for that reason – flouting of contractual policies and obligations."
A spokesperson for Rockstar added: "Rockstar Games' position has been clear and consistent throughout. Individuals across the UK and Canada were dismissed for gross misconduct following the sharing of confidential company information, not because of alleged trade union membership or activity. The tribunal has heard our evidence and seen the facts. We remain confident of a positive outcome."
Judge Lucy Wiseman, who oversaw the tribunal, stated that while a timeframe could not yet be given for the judgemen t, she would "use [her] best endeavours to get that judgement out as quickly as possible."

title: The future of British gaming is more than just games | Opinion
author: Jason Kingsley
excerpt:
The UK has one of the most creative and innovative video games industries in the world. From independent studios developing original ideas to established businesses creating globally recognised franchises, British developers have consistently shown that they can compete on the international stage.
Read more
text:
The UK has one of the most creative and innovative video games industries in the world. From independent studios developing original ideas to established businesses creating globally recognised franchises, British developers have consistently shown that they can compete on the international stage.
The Government rightly recognises the creative industries as a priority growth sector, and over the past two decades we’ve seen a significant improvement in how policymakers engage with our industry. There is now a much greater understanding of the economic contribution games make, the highly skilled jobs they support and their potential as a major British export.
But as the industry evolves, we need to ensure the policies designed to support it evolve too.
We have an opportunity to have a much bigger conversation about how the UK supports the development and ownership of British intellectual property.
Entertainment is changing
Traditionally, video games, film, television and publishing have been treated as distinct industries, each with their own business models, funding structures and tax incentives. Now the boundaries between them are becoming blurred.
A successful video game can become a hit television series . A comic book character can inspire a major film franchise. A compelling fictional universe can find audiences across multiple formats, platforms and generations. At Rebellion, this is something we understand first-hand.
The Rogue Trooper IP began in the 2000AD comics before becoming a game in 2006 and a movie this year. | Image credit: Rebellion/Liberty Films
Alongside developing and publishing video games, we own 2000 AD, the home of iconic characters including Judge Dredd and Rogue Trooper. We also operate across comics, books, film and television, bringing stories and characters to life in different ways. Our recent Rogue Trooper film is an example of how intellectual property can move between creative formats, reaching new audiences while building on an established British franchise.
For businesses like ours, these aren't separate industries. They're different expressions of the same underlying intellectual property, supported by teams of talented people working across disciplines.
Yet the UK's system of creative tax reliefs remains largely organised around individual formats. We have incentives for video games, film, television and other forms of production, but comparatively little recognition of the intellectual property that connects them.
Backing British IP
Creating a successful game, character or fictional universe can take years of investment, experimentation and risk. But when an idea succeeds, its value can extend well beyond the format in which it was originally created. For British studios, the opportunity is to build the next globally recognised entertainment franchise and, critically, to retain ownership of that intellectual property here in the UK.
Related
New Remedy CEO discusses prioritising own IP and learning from its mistakes
"Honestly, we haven't achieved half of the potential in terms of the products that we make," says Jean-Charles Gaudechon
We only need to look across the Atlantic to see the potential. American entertainment giants like Disney and Marvel have built global businesses around characters and stories that span films, television, games and publishing. There is no reason why Britain cannot build more businesses with similar ambitions, developing homegrown intellectual property into franchises that reach audiences around the world.
When British businesses own their IP, they have greater control over how it is developed, licensed and commercialised. They can reinvest the returns into new projects, create skilled jobs and build sustainable businesses that continue to generate value over decades. This is particularly important for independent developers, who often face difficult decisions about how to fund ambitious projects while retaining control of the ideas they create.
There is no simple solution, and any reform would need to recognise the different economics of games, film, television and publishing. But I believe there is a strong case for the Government to explore how existing creative tax incentives could better support businesses developing intellectual property across multiple formats.
That means asking whether the framework we have today properly reflects how modern creative businesses operate, and whether it does enough to encourage long-term investment in British-owned IP.
The future of the industry
The UK already has many of the ingredients needed to build the next generation of global entertainment franchises, like exceptional creative talent, world-class studios, a strong independent development community and a rich history of storytelling.
The challenge now is ensuring that the businesses creating those franchises have the support and confidence to scale internationally while remaining rooted in Britain.
Government engagement with the games industry has come a long way, and that progress should be recognised. Now we have an opportunity to build on it. If we want Britain to remain a global leader in creative innovation, we need to think beyond individual games, films or television productions, and recognise the long-term value of the intellectual property that connects them.

title: US Senate hearing examines child safety on Roblox, considers bipartisan bill to bypass forced arbitration
author: Sophie McEvoy
excerpt:
The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing this week to examine child safety on Roblox and consider a bipartisan bill that would allow families and victims to bypass forced arbitration.
Read more
text:
The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing this week to examine child safety on Roblox and consider a bipartisan bill that would allow families and victims to bypass forced arbitration.
As Bloomberg reports, the No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act, introduced by Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin, would allow those affected to pursue legal action in public court, even if they previously agreed to private arbitration in a company's terms of use.
In response, Roblox global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço told Wired : "Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat."
"A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company's safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety. Protecting children online takes stronger protections, better tools, and consistent standards that apply everywhere kids spend time online."
During the hearing, Senator Hawley criticised Roblox's child safety record, stating it failed to address issues because doing so would "threaten their user count, and therefore their revenues."
"If your children are on Roblox, they are being exposed in all likelihood to sexual predators," he added.
Roblox CEO David Baszucki declined to testify in court. In a letter obtained by Bloomberg, he stated that "Roblox continues to welcome the discussion of how online platforms protect young people online."
"Online safety cannot be solved by any one company. Bad actors move between platforms, and a child's online life spans many apps, games, and services."
The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism began its investigation into Roblox in August, requesting records related to child safety, sexual or physical abuse, bullying, and financial exploitation.
In a letter to Baszucki, Hawley and Durbin said the "alleged criminal activity on Roblox warrants congressional scrutiny."
"You trumpet Roblox as a safe digital playground for children as young as five," the senators wrote. "But the public record raises serious questions about this promise of safety."
"Over the past decade, police have arrested numerous individuals for committing serious acts of violence and harm against children they met via Roblox, including grooming , sexual abuse , kidnapping , rape , and even murder [...] children on your platform are hurting. Congress will not look the other way."
Roblox has implemented several new safety tools in recent years, such as restricting users under 13 from direct messaging , introducing global facial recognition checks , adding a "sensitive issues" content tag for experiences, and strengthening moderation policies and actions .
html:
The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing this week to examine child safety on Roblox and consider a bipartisan bill that would allow families and victims to bypass forced arbitration.

As Bloomberg reports, the No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act, introduced by Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin, would allow those affected to pursue legal action in public court, even if they previously agreed to private arbitration in a company's terms of use.

In response, Roblox global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço told Wired: "Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat."

"A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company's safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety. Protecting children online takes stronger protections, better tools, and consistent standards that apply everywhere kids spend time online."

During the hearing, Senator Hawley criticised Roblox's child safety record, stating it failed to address issues because doing so would "threaten their user count, and therefore their revenues."

"If your children are on Roblox, they are being exposed in all likelihood to sexual predators," he added.

Roblox CEO David Baszucki declined to testify in court. In a letter obtained by Bloomberg, he stated that "Roblox continues to welcome the discussion of how online platforms protect young people online."

"Online safety cannot be solved by any one company. Bad actors move between platforms, and a child's online life spans many apps, games, and services."

The US Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism began its investigation into Roblox in August, requesting records related to child safety, sexual or physical abuse, bullying, and financial exploitation.

In a letter to Baszucki, Hawley and Durbin said the "alleged criminal activity on Roblox warrants congressional scrutiny."

"You trumpet Roblox as a safe digital playground for children as young as five," the senators wrote. "But the public record raises serious questions about this promise of safety."

"Over the past decade, police have arrested numerous individuals for committing serious acts of violence and harm against children they met via Roblox, including grooming, sexual abuse, kidnapping, rape, and even murder [...] children on your platform are hurting. Congress will not look the other way."

Roblox has implemented several new safety tools in recent years, such as restricting users under 13 from direct messaging, introducing global facial recognition checks, adding a "sensitive issues" content tag for experiences, and strengthening moderation policies and actions.

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 debuts as top-selling game in US for October 2026
author: Sophie McEvoy
excerpt:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 led US sales in October according to Circana, marking the 19th consecutive year a Call of Duty title has been the best-selling game during its launch month.
Read more
text:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 led US sales in October according to Circana, marking the 19th consecutive year a Call of Duty title has been the best-selling game during its launch month.
The game, which was generally well received by critics , beat two other new releases in October's Top 5 – Gears of War: E-Day in second and Star Wars: Galactic Racer in third.
There were six new releases overall, including Final Fantasy Resonance (No.6), Kingdom Hearts Collection 2 – 3 (No.9) and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (No.10).
Control Resonant moved into the top 10, from No.11 to No.8, following its physical release on October 15. The game launched digitally on September 24, and has become Remedy's fastest-selling title to date .
Total US video game spending declined 12% in October to $4.2 billion. Circana attributed this to a 14% drop in content sales to $3.7 billion, primarily due to a 16% decrease in mobile.
Console content spending fell 18% year-on-year, reflecting the impact of major releases Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A in the previous period.
Hardware spending increased 2% year-on-year to $357 million, with 42% growth in Xbox Series sales and 20% growth in PlayStation 5. These gains offset an 11% drop in Nintendo Switch 2 sales.
Circana attributed PS5 and Xbox Series growth to higher prices. PS5 unit sales increased 5% with a 13% rise in average selling price. Xbox Series unit sales grew 10%, and its average selling price rose 29%.
Switch 2 led hardware in both unit and dollar sales for October and year-to-date 2026, with PS5 ranking second.

title: 007 First Light wins GOTY at 2026 TIGA Awards, Dovetail Games takes home four accolades including Best Publisher
author: Sophie McEvoy
excerpt:

text:
IO Interactive's 007 First Light received Game of the Year at the 2026 TIGA Awards, while Dovetail Games earned four awards, including Best Publisher and Best Educational, Serious or Simulation Game for Train Sim World 6.
The Chatham-based studio also won Commitment to ESG and Commitment to Workplace Wellbeing.
Playground Games won Best Large Studio and Best In-House Recruitment and Talent Development, while Wales Interactive received Best Small Studio and Best VR/AR/XR/MR Game for Maid of Sker VR.
London-based indie studio SFB Games' The Mermaid Mask was recognised for Creativity in Games and Best Narrative/Storytelling.
Elsewhere, Crimson Desert won Best Action and Adventure Game, and Ghost of Yōtei received Best Visual Design.
Side was recognised as Best Services Provider and QA/Localisation Provider, while Room 8 Group won Best Co-Development Partner, and Code Wizards Group received Best Technical Innovation.
The Outstanding Leadership award was presented to Steel City Interactive CEO Ash Habib, and the Outstanding Individual of the Year award was given to Associate Professor Mark Wickham, Director of Computer Arts and Technology at Norwich University of the Arts and TIGA Education Advisor.
Wickham was recognised for "his contribution to games education, his support for TIGA's work to strengthen links between education and industry and his contribution to TIGA's accreditation system."
"These awards recognise the talent and dedication involved in making outstanding games, building successful businesses and delivering excellence in games education," said TIGA CEO Richard Wilson.

title: Ubisoft lays off 166 staff in Montreal and Quebec studios
author: Jon Hicks
excerpt:
Ubisoft is laying off staff in its vast Montreal and Quebec studios, with 166 roles being lost "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."
Read more
text:
Ubisoft is laying off staff in its vast Montreal and Quebec studios, with 166 roles being lost "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."
GamesIndustry.biz understands that the affected positions were chiefly in production and support roles, and represented less than 4% of the total headcount at the studios. The layoffs impacted employees working on projects that had recently been cancelled or significantly changed. The firm did not refer to any impact on specific games or projects under development at the studios, which work on some of the firm's largest gaming brands.
"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," the company said in a statement provided to GamesIndustry.biz . "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."
"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."
GamesIndustry.biz understands that the cuts include members of Vantage Studios , the joint venture with Tencent that houses the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Rainbow Six franchises. Vantage is a Creative House within Ubisoft's new business structure , which was announced at the start of the year alongside a "final" round of cuts to deliver €200 million in savings. The firm has cut hundreds of jobs and closed multiple studios over the course of the year, including Ubisoft Winnipeg, Ubisoft RedLynx, Ubisoft Belgrade and Ubisoft Halifax.
The firm renamed Creative House 2 as Massive Entertainment in September, following the appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Cristoph Hartmann as head of the unit, and cut staff across its German offices in October.

title: PlayStation emerges victorious in a $2.6 billion lawsuit alleging a digital monopoly
author: Imran Khan
excerpt: The now-dismissed lawsuit accused PlayStation of setting "excessive and unfair prices" in the UK, but will not proceed any further.
text:
The now-dismissed lawsuit accused PlayStation of setting "excessive and unfair prices" in the UK, but will not proceed any further.
A $2.6 billion class action lawsuit brought in the United Kingdom against PlayStation has been dismissed by London's Competition Appeal Tribunal, clearing PlayStation of unfair practices that were alleged when the lawsuit was filed in 2023, noted by VGC .
The lawsuit, brought by UK consumer rights activist Alex Neil and representing the UK's 8.9 million PlayStation customers, argued that Sony's 30 percent cut on all digital purchases made on the PlayStation store while also determining prices on said store constitute an abuse of its dominant position and lead to excessive prices.
On the website for the class action , Neill and her lawyers argue that the current dynamic is rife for abuse and Sony is overcharging relative to the costs of these products.
"The business model of gaming has changed dramatically over recent years," the site reads. "The move from games sold as physical disks to games sold digitally has seen the introduction of in-game content, where players must now also pay to progress, unlock more features, or customize their experience with new characters or weapons. Games are now designed to incentivize players to spend as much money as possible (including children)."
Related: Shigeru Miyamoto selected as inaugural Legend Award inductee at DICE Awards
The appeal tribunal did not agree with Neill's arguments, though perhaps not for enduring reasons. Part of the tribunal's reasoning is that PlayStation cannot maintain a monopoly over digital sales when physical sales are a consumer option, production of which PlayStation will be abandoning in 2028 . But overall, the court was not swayed by the argument that PlayStation games were priced too high on the platform's digital store, so it is unlikely the removal of physical games as an option will change the tribunal's minds.
The lawsuit proceeding would have likely forced Sony to adjust its 30 percent fees for video game developers, significantly eroding the platform holder's margins. While the UK lawsuit has been dismissed, similar suits in Australia, Netherlands, Portugal, and the US could still rock the division's foundations if they make significant headway.

title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's narrative lead wants to change game funding
author: Imran Khan
excerpt: After winning numerous awards, Clair Obscur narrative lead Jennifer Svedberg-Yen wants to change the story about priorities in game funding.
text:
After winning numerous awards, Clair Obscur narrative lead Jennifer Svedberg-Yen wants to change the story about priorities in game funding.
The narrative lead behind one of 2025's most critically-acclaimed games , Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, has departed Sandfall after helping catapult Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 to notable success as one of the most awarded video games of all time. A few months after leaving the studio, she wants to change the way that narrative design gets funded and advanced in the game industry.
In a profile piece with GamesBeat , Svedberg-Yen describes a personal goal of reshaping how the industry develops stories and what it does to support, or not support, the creative talent that keeps it aloft. After leaving Sandfall back in July, Svedberg-Yen—who previously worked in finance and private equity—wants to put game narratives first and reverse the common wisdom that treats it as an afterthought during development.
"A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin," Svedberg-Yen told Gamesbeat. "They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense. But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other."
Svedberg-Yen has set up a fund dedicated to advancing the art of narrative design and create new funding models focused on curating and nurturing talent.
Related: What Rami Ismail learned during his return to game development
"I’m not trying to compete with publishers," Svedberg-Yen explains. "But I’m trying to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make."
Sverberg-Yen has not yet detailed exactly how the fund will work, but emphasizes that it's one of her main focuses in 2027, alongside her own projects.
"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry," she says."

title: Why greenlighting Dressmaker wasn't an easy decision to make
author: Bryant Francis
excerpt: Pre-production data said Dressmaker might not find an audience. Free Lives pushed past those numbers to make a bona fide hit.
text:
Pre-production data said Dressmaker might not find an audience. Free Lives pushed past those numbers to make a bona fide hit.
Cozy Lives and Free Lives' Dressmaker is the surprise sleeper indie hit of 2026. It's racked up thousands of 'overwhelmingly positive' reviews on Steam and driven conversation among developers about how the industry may be missing out on certain audiences by ignoring different types of gameplay. But while it's got tongues wagging now, there was a moment in pre-production where its makers weren't sure the game would actually find its audience.
That's according to Dressmaker programmer and designer Ruan Rothman, who explained to GameDeveloper.com that Free Lives has spent years building a process to identify game ideas that are creatively interesting and have commercial viability. Answering the question of "what game to make" may seem obvious, but it can be a daunting task for game developers. Just because you're excited about a game, does it mean that there's an audience who will share your passion?
Related: Zelda and Grand Theft Auto headline the nominees for the 2027 Game Awards
And even if there's an audience, can you make the game in a way that fits an appropriate scope and budget? Savvy developers everywhere have long sought ways to mitigate the risks that come with the hit-driven nature of video game development—and Free Lives' process begins with releasing prototypes on Itch.io .
Free Lives uses game jams and itch prototypes to blend passion and commercial potential
Free Lives built its process based on a concept almost everyone in the game industry can relate to: nobody can "reliably intuitively tell" whether a game can be creatively and commercially viable. So in the last few years, the studio adopted "a set of heuristics" to help judge which games were worth pursuing.
"We try to be as empirical as possible in our approach," Rothman explained in a conversation that came after we spoke with him and artist Sara Laubscher on the GameDeveloper.com podcast . "Every pitch needs a playable prototype, usually hosted on itch.io. The first test is whether the prototype gains traction on that platform, specifically regarding engagement and downloads."
"The second [test] is whether the game gets a response on social media, so we might create a mini-trailer or post gameplay clips online to gauge the response. Finally, if content creators spontaneously create videos of the game (usually YouTube), that's another great signal. Even more compelling, is when the videos of your game/prototype are overperforming on those channels relative to the average views the content creator gets." He noted that the team is aware this process risks burning through a game's marketing momentum. If an influencer plays the early prototype two years before the game comes out, interest in the game can be hard to maintain or "regenerate."
Related: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick says GTA VI needs to be 'marketed aggressively' despite global brand awareness
Image via Cozy Lives/Free Lives
These aren't "hard and fast rules," he said, so subjective judgment remains "inevitable" in the process. But the stakes are high. "The worst possible outcome in game development is spending years on a game that nobody wants," Rothman said. "Besides the obvious financial implications, even if your studios survives, it's devastating for morale."
With so much adoration that's greeted Dressmaker since it made its public debut, you'd think there was existing interest built on that process. According to Rothman, that wasn't the case, and the question of whether or not to proceed with development required discussion and debate. The first Dressmaker prototype that emerged from Free Lives' internal game jam "wasn't quite playable," but was sufficient to make test posts on Instagram. The reaction justified the decision to then greenlight a free itch.io-ready prototype, eventually scoring 10,000 downloads in its first month on the platform.
Unfortunately that's a relatively low number for Free Lives' prototypes. Another of its games, Stick it to the Stickman racked up over 100,000 downloads. There wasn't any organic content creator uptake, and no publishers reached out to discuss signing the title. This all made the "signal" of Dressmaker difficult to understand, especially since the Free Lives team had never made a "cozy game" before.
Related: Twitch will sacrifice you to its AI overlord whether you like it or not
Despite the low numbers, there was reason to keep testing. Because even though Stick it to the Stickman was downloaded more often, it wound up "underperforming" after being released on Steam. Ruan said it made the Free Lives team wonder if itch.io was still a "reliable predictor" for Steam success.
So the team initiated another marketing push on social media and reached out for a few influencers. Again, the response on Instagram and TikTok seemed to show there was an audience out there excited about a dressmaking game, so they decided to proceed cautiously ahead under a "limited" scope. Luckily, it paid off in spades.
What's the lesson from a surprise hit?
By now you've probably heard over and over again how "data-driven approaches" are essential to succeed in the modern game industry. Except in the case of Dressmaker , the data was telling a story that could have gone one way or another. So it's worth asking—does Rothman think the Free Lives team learned anything from this experience?
"I don't think we've figured that out just yet!" he admitted. "We now know that you need multiple corroborating signals in order to trust that a project has appeal, and that any one single metric can be quite unreliable. We've had some prototypes get great traction on social media, but then fail to convert to prototype downloads or success on Steam."
Keep in mind that Free Lives isn't some big publisher looking to turn game development into a factory line process with perfectly-predicted marketing. Rothman said the studio is filled with people who want to make "culturally relevant, standout hit games." "We don't want to simply tread water by breaking even on a project to project basis," he said.
Ironically, that means the search for stability—even when backed by a data-driven approach—means planning to take risks. Rothmann said Free Lives' next games are "likely to again, be so completely different than anything else we've done."
"And the development scene is changing faster than ever before," he added. "So who knows?"

title: 经历4811天后，至少我们还有《GTA 6》
author: 祝佳音
text:
《Grand Theft Auto VI》（GTA 6）今天（2026年11月19日）发售了。它的上一代是2013年9月17日发售的，距今天13年2个月零2天，或者说，4811天。
一款游戏和它的续作之间相距13年——这个时间是如此之长，以至于很难让人第一时间产生实感。我们度过了怎样的13年？13年之后，我们的世界已经完全不一样了。
发售于2013年的《侠盗猎车手V》设定在2013年-2014年的圣安地列斯州 (San Andreas)
2013年《GTA 5》发售时的新闻配图，“这款游戏卖得比历史上任何一款电子游戏、电影或其他娱乐产品都要快“（图源：Reuters Mike Blake）
在2013年时，还没有OpenAI和Anthropic。字节跳动在1年前（2012年3月）刚刚成立，距离TikTok推出还有4年。当时的科技明星是Facebook，它正在快速扩张，苹果处于乔布斯去世后的产品与文化转型期，Google则代表着硅谷新经济的另一种理想主义。这些公司以一种杂糅的方式出现在《GTA 5》里，成了被讽刺的对象。游戏里有把发布会包装成宗教仪式的科技公司iFruit（显然，嘲讽的就是苹果）和几乎就是Facebook翻版的Lifeinvader。无论在游戏里还是游戏外，公司的高管们都在向人们描绘着美好的未来，而他们现在正在竭尽全力让自己在AI狂潮中不被落下。
《GTA 5》中的iFruit手机
现在看来有些陌生的仿Facebook界面（《GTA 5》中的Lifeinvader）
在《GTA 5》里，角色们使用的手机看起来像是iPhone，那时候苹果手机刚出到5s/5c，现在它已经到了18和Duo——虽然18的外形看起来仍然没什么大变化。特斯拉的两款电动车也出现在《GTA 5》里，它们是化名为Coil Voltic的Tesla Roadster和化名为Coil Raiden的Tesla Model S。这也是特斯拉当时仅有的两款量产车型。2013年的洛圣都路上仍然以燃油车为主。特斯拉2013年底的市值约为185亿美元，现在它的市值是1.54万亿美元，约为当年的83倍。但这比起英伟达算不上什么。《GTA 5》推出那年，英伟达的市值约为91亿美元，现在，《GTA 6》推出的这个月，在几次震荡之后，英伟达的市值约为4.8-5.0万亿美元，在13年间，它的市值增长了约550倍。
化名为Coil Voltic的Tesla Roadster
同样是在这13年里，黄金的价格从约250每克一度上涨到超过1000元每克，现在则在每克830元左右震荡。2013年时，一枚比特币的价格约为140美元，后来则一度突破10万美元。同样是2013年，《GTA 5》推出的时候，中国的GDP总值约为9.6万亿美元，13年后这个数字是大约19万亿美元。
数据来源：World Bank
《GTA 5》推出时，巴拉克·奥巴马正处于他的第二个美国总统任期中，然后是唐纳德·特朗普，再然后是拜登，再然后是特朗普的第二个任期。同样是在2013年，英国首相是卡梅伦，在此之后，英国在13年里换了6任首相，现在的英国首相叫安迪·伯纳姆，他是7月上台的。《GTA 5》推出时，乌克兰人民还在为是否与欧盟签联系国协定争论，当时的总统是亚努科维奇。11月，乌克兰爆发广场革命，2019年，泽连斯基当选乌克兰总统，2022年，全面战争爆发。
2013年到2026年间，人类经历了一场持续数年的全球性疫情。2020年至2022年，我们的日常生活和社会活动在不同程度上受到限制。全球人口的生活方式和社会交往方式都发生了显著变化。2013年，《GTA 5》推出的时候，全球化仍然是大多数人所相信的时代叙事。我们相信互联网会链接所有人，全球贸易会让各国共同富裕，技术会逐步消除地域和文化隔阂。而今天相信这些的人已经不多了。
2013年的时候，全球游戏产业正迎来因移动设备普及而带来的大量新用户。在中国，资本和游戏开发者们刚刚经历了网页游戏的大崩溃，我们面对着移动设备普及所带来的无尽蓝海！游戏开发者们第一次享受到了70%的收入分成（在此之前是30%甚至10%）和几乎不拖欠的付款周期。中国的移动游戏行业高速爆发，并由此开始了现在刚入行的从业者几乎难以想象的几年好日子。此时，距离腾讯的《王者荣耀》出现还有2年，距离网易的《阴阳师》出现还有3年，距离米哈游的《原神》上线还有7年。
《GTA 5》就像今天的《GTA 6》一样在PlayStation平台上首发，只不过一个是3，一个是5。当时的Steam最高同时在线人数只有约800万人，现在这个数字是4000万以上，使用简体中文的用户约占活跃账户的33.7%。
2013年至2025年7月，《GTA 5》在Steam上的月度最高同时在线玩家人数变化，单位为千人（数据来源：Statista）
当年，当中国玩家对着《GTA 5》赞叹的时候，并没有多少人会想到，11年之后，我们终于迎来了真正意义上的国产3A作品——这个时间看起来那么长，但又让人感觉好像也没那么长。2024年，《黑神话：悟空》发布，2026年，《影之刃零》发布。我们终于踏出了这一步。
2013年时，版号制度尚未覆盖到移动游戏，2016年5月，国家新闻出版广电总局发布通知，规定移动游戏上线前必须取得版号。在此之后，中国游戏行业迎来了两次9个月左右未发版号的日子，大批游戏公司注销，从业者另谋他路。而现在版号每月照常发放，已经不再成为需要报道的新闻。在这13年间，中国游戏产业的规模从2013年的约831亿增长到约4000亿元。然而就我所见，从业者们似乎并没有比13年前更快乐、轻松，或充满希望。
2016年，国家新闻出版广电总局发布移动游戏出版服务管理新规，国产移动游戏上线运营前须按规定提交出版申请，《出版国产移动游戏作品申请表》成为版号申报材料之一
比起2013年，我们都老了13岁。现在我们已经发现自己并不是不死的，我们也会疲惫，也会长久被病痛折磨。我们也会发现病痛和疲劳并不会在一场熟睡后的第二天清晨自己消失得无影无踪，我们也和其他人一样会眼花、腰疼，或者长久感到疲惫。我们也会犯傻、后悔、犯错，或者作出让自己遗憾终身的选择。有人迎来了新生命，也有人的家人和朋友在这13年间离我们而去。同样离开我们的还有岩田聪、鸟山明、坂本龙一、斯蒂芬·霍金、伊丽莎白二世、大卫·鲍伊、罗宾·威廉姆斯（他很可能玩GTA系列）、金庸，以及更多的人。就在现在看这篇文章的人中，也有一些人未来再也没有机会玩到《GTA 7》了。
但至少我们迎来了《GTA 6》。你玩过《GTA 5》，你经历了这么多，现在仍然等着进入《GTA 6》的世界——你已经等了它好几年了，这期间你一度忘记了它，但它现在回来了。你已经下好了游戏，把手柄充满电，坐在沙发上，盯着电视，那个可以让自己短暂忘记烦恼的世界正在准备迎接你——就像13年前一样。所以恭喜你，朋友，在这个一切都在不停变化的世界上，我们至少拥有了一些不变的东西。
“至少我们还有GTA”
html:
《Grand Theft Auto VI》（GTA 6）今天（2026年11月19日）发售了。它的上一代是2013年9月17日发售的，距今天13年2个月零2天，或者说，4811天。

一款游戏和它的续作之间相距13年——这个时间是如此之长，以至于很难让人第一时间产生实感。我们度过了怎样的13年？13年之后，我们的世界已经完全不一样了。

在2013年时，还没有OpenAI和Anthropic。字节跳动在1年前（2012年3月）刚刚成立，距离TikTok推出还有4年。当时的科技明星是Facebook，它正在快速扩张，苹果处于乔布斯去世后的产品与文化转型期，Google则代表着硅谷新经济的另一种理想主义。这些公司以一种杂糅的方式出现在《GTA 5》里，成了被讽刺的对象。游戏里有把发布会包装成宗教仪式的科技公司iFruit（显然，嘲讽的就是苹果）和几乎就是Facebook翻版的Lifeinvader。无论在游戏里还是游戏外，公司的高管们都在向人们描绘着美好的未来，而他们现在正在竭尽全力让自己在AI狂潮中不被落下。

在《GTA 5》里，角色们使用的手机看起来像是iPhone，那时候苹果手机刚出到5s/5c，现在它已经到了18和Duo——虽然18的外形看起来仍然没什么大变化。特斯拉的两款电动车也出现在《GTA 5》里，它们是化名为Coil Voltic的Tesla Roadster和化名为Coil Raiden的Tesla Model S。这也是特斯拉当时仅有的两款量产车型。2013年的洛圣都路上仍然以燃油车为主。特斯拉2013年底的市值约为185亿美元，现在它的市值是1.54万亿美元，约为当年的83倍。但这比起英伟达算不上什么。《GTA 5》推出那年，英伟达的市值约为91亿美元，现在，《GTA 6》推出的这个月，在几次震荡之后，英伟达的市值约为4.8-5.0万亿美元，在13年间，它的市值增长了约550倍。

title: 触乐夜话：我和我的GTA
author: 祝佳音
text:
触乐夜话，每天胡侃和游戏有关的屁事、鬼事、新鲜事。
图/小罗
真是奇怪呀，在我的回忆里，几乎我所有和GTA有关的记忆都是在工作岗位上。
我第一次接触GTA的时候就是3。当时我还在《大众软件》杂志社旗下的《大众游戏》杂志工作。XBOX刚出，我们有一位在美国的朋友在当地买了XBOX，千里迢迢寄到编辑部。游戏机有了，但只有一张附带的《光环》。当时我们还不习惯用手柄玩FPS（其实现在也不习惯），玩了一阵，总是感觉很难投入。也就逐渐放下了。一直到了那年春节，我回到哈尔滨去过年。作为一个传统节日习俗，哈尔滨的游戏爱好者在春节的时候都要去位于哈工大附近的教化电子大世界购买盗版游戏盘——北京当年买盗版盘特别困难，要在中关村一带的胡同里和抱着孩子的妇女接头，对暗号，跟着走恨不得800米才能买到，哈尔滨就不一样了，教化电子大世界一楼有几百个摊位，全都卖盗版盘，每个摊位上有几千张盗版盘，人头攒动，熙熙攘攘，非常壮观。
有时候我也在想，如果我不是因为高中时学校附近就是这个市场，我得以疯狂购买廉价光盘，爽玩所有游戏，一定程度上也算增长了眼界；或者，如果不是因为我初中时学校到家的那一条路上遍布二手书摊，哈尔滨当时正值下岗，工人们就把工厂阅读室里的书拿出来卖，售价极便宜，我每天都买一两本，拼命看完，第二天就能买新的——如果不是因为这些，我是否还会从事文字工作？是否还会做游戏媒体这个行当？又或者，如果我的家里人不是恰好还算有些文化，还能给我比较早的买电脑和让我上网，我是否还会做这一行呢？我们所谓的成绩，有多少是归功于自己，有多少又是归功于运气呢？
还是说回到那年春节的教化电子大世界，我当时对GTA一无所知，还以为是GT赛车呢，GT赛车开头也是G，GTA开头也是G，如何买不得？于是我就买了一堆盘，带回北京。其他的游戏有什么我都忘记了，GTA我一玩就喜欢上了。当时编辑部里有一台彩监，我们也无所谓上班下班，工作时间，反正谁想玩就去玩，我就在单位断断续续玩通了《GTA 3》。
看看当年《GTA 3》的画面
我后来经常也感叹，GTA就是美国。GTA的文化就建立在美国文化传播全球的基础上，GTA里的世界观、价值观和行事风格在全世界通行无阻，基本没有传播隔阂，这都是因为美国的文化作品在此前以统治的姿态畅行全世界，任何人来到GTA的世界里都会觉得很熟悉，这种感觉正是无数电影、电视剧和书籍打下的底子。按现在的说法，这也算是一种文化霸权，所以从这个角度，我对“中国人的现代题材开放世界”感觉有点复杂，一方面，这种游戏类型也像是植物成熟后就一定会结出果实一样必然会出现，另一方面，我觉得它距离在全世界传播也还有一些时日。
我当时不太玩得明白《GTA 3》，但是我真的喜欢这个游戏。我在当时的《大众游戏》办公室玩它，几乎每天上班时间都玩它。其实我后来才意识到很多人并不那么喜欢它，有些人不喜欢这个题材，有些人不习惯开车，这也都很正常，我就不喜欢所有的动作游戏，可能是我手笨，无论是忍龙、魂系，还是“怪物猎人”，甚至黑神话和影之刃，我都不太能融入，游戏都是好游戏，但我就是玩不好。可GTA不一样，我和它仿佛天生合适。我喜欢在游戏里开车，也喜欢现代武器，也喜欢现实主义题材——虽然GTA并不完全是现实主义题材而我觉得更类似北美魔幻现实题材，但它也很对我的胃口！对了，同样是Rockstar，《荒野大镖客 2》我就没玩通，由此可见我喜欢车胜过马。
我玩通了《GTA 3》，所谓玩通，就是把剧情打完了吧，看得一知半解。后来又玩了“罪恶都市”和“圣安德列斯”，我更喜欢罪恶都市，其实我也没怎么看过《疤面煞星》，不知道为什么，我更喜欢罪恶都市的气氛。相较而言我就没那么喜欢圣安德列斯，虽然也玩了，但是感受并不特别深。相较而言罪恶都市的气氛我就很喜欢，我经常漫无目的地在里面找一辆车，然后在遍布霓虹灯的迈阿密街头就只是单纯地开车。
《GTA 4》我玩得不太多，可能是故事不吸引人？或者是我当时的工作比较忙？总之我没有留下什么印象，我认识的很多人对4的故事评价很高，但其实我确实感觉不太深。
然后就是《GTA 5》——它和触乐同年出生，唉，看看人家！那时候我们刚刚建立触乐，买了一台60寸的小米电视放在办公室里，我还从家里拿了PS4，然后就在办公室玩它。在游戏媒体的办公室里玩游戏，不但是理所当然，简直是天经地义，还兼具展示效果，所以其实一想到《GTA 6》，我就想起我们当年的快乐时光。
《GTA 6》重回Vice City
《GTA 5》基本可以说是集3A游戏之大成的作品了，我真的挑不出它的什么问题来。而且我尤其喜欢里面的角色——这次有官方汉化版了，它的剧情真不错啊，我一直觉得麦克就是开发者的化身，年轻的时候有活力，有钱，但这些都不能阻止他慢慢地变老，对很多事情看不惯但知道他已经不是世界的主角了，于是他这个人就弥漫着一股淡淡的中年死意。我虽然没什么证据，但坚信剧情设计师把自己放在了麦克的身上。我现在也对很多情节有印象，认真想想，这已经是13年前的事情啦。
我很满意我现在仍然对《GTA 6》感兴趣，我也真的希望我能活着看到《GTA 7》，我很好奇，玩到《GTA 7》的时候我会是什么样？是否变得愤世嫉俗？或者变成那种让人讨厌的老登？登峰造极的那种？或者成为一个印第安纳琼斯博士，在埃及继续挖掘外星人飞船——我希望是后一种！但也有可能我在病床上弥留，又或者根本看不到续作就去世了，谁知道呢！
