多重计算视角下的推论和阐释 Multicomputational Implications & Interpretation
我们已经考察了许多游戏和谜题的例子。在每一个例子中，我们都探索了囊括了整个可能行为谱系的多路图。那么，我们的结论是什么呢？
最明显的一点是，如果游戏和谜题在我们看来是困难的——或者说是「有趣的」——它在某种程度上为多路图的显著复杂性所反映。或者，换句话说，当我们发现多路图在某种程度上「难以解码（decode）」时，我们就会得到一个丰富的、吸引人的游戏或谜题。
在玩一个游戏的任何特定实例中，我们基本上是沿着一条特定的路径（与物理学相类似，我们可以称之为「时间路径（timelike path）」）穿过游戏的多路图（或「游戏图」）。并且在某种程度上，我们可能只是做了一个全局性的声明，即游戏图代表了所有这样的路径。
但多重计算范式（Multicomputational paradigm）所建议的是，我们还可以有效地做出更多的局部声明。特别是，在沿着一条时间路径的每一步，我们可以在多路图中「横断地（transversally）」观察，并看到「瞬时分支图」，它代表了我们的路径与「邻近路径」的「纠缠（entanglement）」。
从而，某种意义上说，弄清「下一步该做什么」就是决定在分支空间中「朝什么方向」走。而游戏的困难之处在于，我们无法轻易预知我们「穿越分支空间」时发生了什么。这里有一个与计算的不可还原性（computational Irreducibility）概念的某种类比。沿着一些时间路径从一个状态到另一个状态，计算的不可还原性意味着，即使我们可能知道根本的规则，我们也不能轻易地预测其结果——因为这可能需要不可减少的计算量来计算出许多步骤之后的结果。
预测「穿越分支空间」是一个相关的、但稍有不同的现象，人们可以将其描述为「多重计算的不可还原性（multicomputational irreducibility）」。这不是关于计算出一个特定路径的困难，而是关于看到许多纠缠的路径如何相互作用的困难。
当一个人在玩游戏时，通常会谈论「能往前看到多少步」。而在我们这里，这基本上是在问我们可以轻易获知能在分支空间里走多远。作为计算上受约束的实体（computationally bounded entities），我们在分支空间有一定的「触达范围」。如果这个范围不足以达到类似「获胜点」的地方，那么这个游戏对我们来说就是「困难的」。
不过，这里还有一个问题。在一个游戏中「获胜」的因素通常是在多路图中达到一些特定的地方或区域。但这些地方或区域的定义通常是一些计算上在约束范围内的东西（「只要看看是否有一行 X」，等等）。这是对系统的某种「观察」，它只是提取了完整状态的一个特定的（计算约束内）采样。然后，关键在于，这个采样并没有设法去「解码多重计算的不可还原性」。
这里有一个与热力学的类比。在热力学中，我们感知到「热」和「熵增加」的事实是这样的：我们的（粗粒度的）度量不能「解码」导致系统中产生的特定状态的不可还原的过程。同样，我们认为「很难弄清楚如何赢得一场游戏」的事实是这样一个结果，即我们的获胜判断标准不能去「观察游戏的内部」和「解码正在发生的事」，直到说它实际上成为只是选择一个特定的、简单径直的路径。相反，它是一个去经历玩游戏的多重计算不可还原的过程的问题，并且相对于对胜利的观察，实际上是「看看它会落在什么位置（seeing where it lands）」。
这里也有一个与量子力学的类比。追溯玩一个游戏的许多可能路径，就像追寻量子力学中的许多历史线程（threads），而获胜的标准就像一个选择某些线程的量子度量。在我们的「物理学计划」中，我们想象我们作为观察者是在分支空间中延伸的，通过我们对自己的单一经验线程的信念，将不同的历史线程「编织在一起」。在游戏中，我们对单一经验线的信念的类比，大概就是「重要的是谁赢谁输；游戏具体是怎么玩的并不重要」。
为了与量子力学做一个更接近的类比，我们可以开始考虑将「多路游玩」的不同部分结合起来，并试图为这些部分如何结合起来制定一套「微积分学」。
我们在这里讨论的游戏在某种意义上都是纯粹的「技巧游戏」。但在也有运气因素的游戏中，我们可以认为这导致了多路图中的单一路径「模糊化（fuzz out）」为一束路径，以及本来是分支空间中的一个点变成了整个扩展区域。
在研究不同的具体游戏和谜题时，我们经常不得不去研究一些相当简化的案例，以便得到规模可控的多路图。但是，如果我们研究非常大的多路图，是否会有整体的规律性涌现？对于游戏图来说，是否存在某种潜在的「连续极限（continuum limit）」？
几乎不可避免的是，如果我们看得「足够详细」，我们就会看到各种多重计算的不可还原性在发挥作用。但在我们的「物理学计划」中，甚至在一般的多重计算范式中，一个关键的问题是，相关的观察者并没有看到那个层次的细节。就像热力学或气体定律从底层分子动力学中的「涌现（emergence ）」一样，底层计算的不可还原性的存在，不可避免地导致观察者所能感知的简单定律。
那么，对于一个游戏来说，「观察者」的类比是什么呢？至少在某些方面，它可以被认为是「获胜」的判断标准。那么现在问题来了：如果我们只看这些标准，我们能不能推导出「物理定律」的类似物，而不敏感于其下的所有多重计算的不可还原的细节？
关于这一点，还有很多东西需要弄清楚，但也许可以从一个地方开始，看看各种游戏中的分支空间和多路图的大规模结构。在许多不同的游戏中，一个基本的印象是，虽然分支图的特征可能在游戏的「不同阶段」之间发生变化，但在单个分支图中，往往有某种统一性。如果我们看一下细节，可能有很多多重计算的不可还原性。但在某种「可感知的水平」上，图的不同部分可能看起来很相似。这表明，即使已经采取了相当不同的行动，将人们带到由分支图定义的「游戏空间」的相当不同部分，「游戏的局部印象」在某一特定阶段往往是相似的，。
但是，虽然分支图的不同部分之间可能存在相似性，但我们看到的是，在一些游戏和谜题中，分支图会分成多个不相连的区域。这反映了游戏中存在着不同的「守恒区（conserved sectors）」——玩家可以进入的游戏空间区域，但随后会被卡住（至少在一定时间内），就像在时空中事件视界（event horizons， 校注：德国天文学家卡尔·史瓦西提出的涉及黑洞的概念，一旦光线或物质越过事件视界，就永远无法逃脱了 ）可以阻止物理空间的不同区域之间的传送。
我们在一些游戏和谜题中注意到的另一个（相关的）现象是多路图中的大「洞」：在图中两点之间有多条「遥远」的路径。当多路图是密集连接的时候，通常总是有办法通过附近的路径改道来 「修复任何错误」。但是，当有一个洞时，这就表明人们最终会「致力于（committed）」某个行动的进程而不是另一个，而且要经过许多步骤才有可能到达与另一个行动进程所能到达的相同的地方。
如果我们假设在某个层面上，我们在多路图中最终「观察」到的是与评估输赢相对应的那种粗粒度，那么我们将不可避免地处理一个可能路径的分布情况。在没有「洞」的情况下，这些路径可能很接近，而且看起来很相似。但是当有洞的时候，可能会有相距甚远的不同的路径。而「属于相同分布部分」的遥远路径可能被认为是类似于量子叠加效应的事实。
游戏中是否有类似于广义相对论和路径积分（path integral）的概念？为了清楚地表述这个问题，我们必须更仔细地定义「游戏空间」的特征。很可能会有因果图（causal graph）的类似物。也很可能游戏空间中也会有一个类似能量的概念，与游戏空间中不同地方的「活动密度」相关。
那么，引力现象的类似物将是这样的：最好的游戏的游玩方式（即通过游戏图的测地路径）将倾向于被高活动密度的存在所偏转。换句话说，如果一个游戏处于某种状态时有很多事要做，那么好的游戏游玩将倾向于「被拉向那个状态」。在某种程度上，这并不令人惊讶：当游戏图中存在高密度的活动时，往往会有更多关于做什么的选择，因此，如果一个玩家经过那里，就更有可能 「玩出一场精彩的游戏」。
到目前为止，我们还没有明确地谈论游戏的策略。但在我们的多重计算框架中，策略有一个相当明确的解释：它是可能规则空间（rulial space）中的一个地方，在那里，人们实际上是假设了一套关于如何构建多路图的规则。换句话说，给定一个策略，人们就会在多路图中选择一些边（或者在相关的多路因果图中选择一些可能的事件），而放弃其他的边。
一般来说，谈论「可能策略的空间」可能很困难，因为这就像谈论「可能程序的空间」。但这恰恰是可能规则空间（rulial space）让我们谈论的东西。「策略空间」到底有什么样的「几何结构」，将取决于我们如何选择协调可能规则空间。但是，再一次，通过仅仅只看类似于博弈论中讨论的那种东西，将倾向于实现某种程度的粗放（coarse-graining）——在这种程度上，我们可以预期所有各种标准的「结构化」的博弈论结果将普遍成立。
（译注：Rulial space 是 Wolfram 自创的一个术语，意指所有可能的规则以及这些规则的所有应用方式所组成的空间。比如，从符号 A 开始应用符号替换规则{A → AB, BB → A}，可以用下面的多路图表示这个规则所有可能的应用方式：
（这个图只画出了前几步，完整的图应该是无限的）
假设只有 A、B 两个符号，只考虑长度最多为 2 的符号串，那么所有这样的可能的替换规则有
按照上面的方式画出所有这些替换规则对应的多路图，并把这些多路图合并成一个图，就构成了这个有限语境下的 Rulial space。
现在想象我们考虑的不仅仅是上面这些符号替换规则，而是宇宙中所有可能的规则，这个巨大的 Rulial Space 可以认为包含了一切”可计算的事物（everything that is computationally possible.）“。推荐阅读： https://writings.stephenwolfram.com/2021/11/the-concept-of-the-ruliad/  ）
个人笔记 Personal Notes
即使在小时候，我也从未特别喜欢玩游戏或做拼图。而这也许是我太像个科学家的一个标志。因为只是选出特定的棋步对我来说总是显得太武断任意了。为了引起我的兴趣，我需要一个更大的图景，更加前后一致的认知叙事。
而现在，从某种意义上说，这正是我在这里讨论的对游戏和谜题的多重计算方法带给我们的东西。是的，能够思考做出特定的动作是非常「人类视角化（humanizing）」的。但是，多重计算方法立即给人了一种连贯的全局观，至少对我来说，理智上更令人满意。
我在这里讨论的探索可以被认为是源于《一种新的科学》中的一个注释。在《一种新的科学》的第五章中，我有一节首次介绍了多路系统。在那一节的最后一个注释中，我讨论了「游戏系统」。
我在 20 世纪 90 年代做了这方面的研究——事实上，我现在发现 1998 年的一本关于井字棋的文件，其中得出了一些相同的结果
其中还有一个看起来很耐人寻味的关于井字棋的图表：
但在那个时候，我并没有从我生成的这些游戏相关的图中得出什么结论；它们只是显得庞大而复杂。20 年过去了，我没有再多想这个问题。但后来在 2017 年，我的儿子克里斯托弗（https://christopherwolfram.com/）在玩一个叫《Rush Hour》的桌游。
也许是家族倾向的表现，他决定构建其游戏图——得出了对我来说似乎是非常令人惊讶的结果。
当时我并没有试图去理解这里的结构，但我还是把它「归档」了，作为游戏图可以有「可见的大规模结构」的证据。
几年后——2019 年底——我们的物理项目正在进行中，我们已经意识到，量子力学和多路图之间存在着深刻的关系。量子力学一直看起来是神秘的东西——纯数学形式主义的抽象结果。但是，看到与多路系统的联系，开始暗示人们实际上能够「理解量子力学」，因为它可以从一些具体的基础结构中「机制地产生」。
我开始思考如何在一个直观的层面上解释量子力学。为此，我需要一个熟悉的类比：可以与多路系统联系起来的日常事物。我立即想到了游戏。2020 年 9 月，我决定考察一下游戏，以更详细地探索这个类比。我很快就分析了井字游戏和尼姆游戏，以及简单的滑动块谜题和汉诺塔。但我想探索更多的游戏和谜题。而且我还有其他项目要做，所以游戏和谜题的多重计算分析被搁置了。
今年早些时候，汉诺塔又出现了，当时我把它作为一个生成类似证明的多路图的例子，与我对元数学的物理化研究有关。最后，几周前我决定是时候写下我到目前为止所知道的关于游戏和谜题的东西了——并产生了这里的东西。
致谢 Thanks
感谢 Brad Klee 和 Ed Pegg 在本文给出的分析的最后阶段提供的各种帮助——以及 Christopher Wolfram 在 2017 年的灵感和 2020 年的帮助。
落日间是一个试图回答「何为游戏」与「游戏何为」的数字人文实验室，我们希望探索一种新的扩展但具体的游戏概念，面对当今游玩化的世界并发掘电子游戏的可能形态。我们正在创作帮助我们理解游戏/电子游戏的文字，音频节目，视频，以及电子游戏（ xpaidia.com ）。

原载简介

本文转自落日间—译介的“自然 - 涌现 - 游戏 Physis - Emergence - Game”分类，译者为厌氧菌，转载已获授权，格式略有调整。

译按

我们知道，复杂系统最重要的特征就是具有涌现行为，简单规则的运用诞生出复杂而难以预测的行为——也就是说，在系统的规则和行为之间存在一种认知鸿沟（Epistemic gap）。

这种认知鸿沟能有多大？鸿沟对面的那个世界究竟有多复杂？我们能够在这些问题上作出某种程度上的比较，甚至量化的计算吗？

除了一种单纯的好奇心在促使我们作出这样的发问，这个问题还有更加现实的意义。复杂系统有很多实际应用。在游戏设计中，游戏规则的涌现行为使得一个游戏具有深度和趣味性；在计算创意学中，创作机制的涌现行为决定了我们在多大程度上可以将这个系统看作是具有想象力的。我们有办法去比较两个游戏谁更有深度，或者两个自动创作系统谁更具想象力吗？

Wolfram 的这篇文章，提出了一种可视化和具体探讨涌现行为的丰富程度的思路——也就是多重计算过程（Multicomputational Process）的概念。作者以几个传统的游戏或者说谜题为例，在计算机的强大算力下得以用图（Graph）的方式去可视化这些游戏规则下的可能游玩路线。能够将游戏规则的深度与这些图的许多直观特征挂钩，也得以将一些图论中早已建立的理论迁移到对游戏趣味性的讨论语境下。我们能在这些图上直接「看到」一个游戏有多有趣、有多难、对哪个玩家更有利——更重要的是，这个游戏规则所构建的系统有多复杂。

在我们已经感受到许多看似简单的游戏竟有着如此令人叹为观止的复杂性之后，作者又引出 Rulial space（所有可能的规则以及这些规则的所有应用方式所组成的空间）的概念，让我们去想象可计算的宇宙这个复杂系统，其复杂程度又形成了怎样的一种维度碾压。这足以让一个并没有在仰望星空的人，也在「宇宙的浩瀚」之下哑口失言。

我作为一个 AI 研究者，虽然很早就接触到诸如基于蒙特卡洛树搜索和加强学习的游戏 AI，以及神经网络或遗传算法生成游戏规则之类的计算机技术，但这篇文章让我第一次感叹，我们做的是一些多么大胆的「试图与宇宙通灵」的事情。

厌氧菌

校按

我是在尝试使用 Wolfram 语言和理解其创始人庞大，且业已进入工业化和商业可持续道路的愿景中发现了这篇文章的，我立刻意识到这是非常有趣的和稀有的研究尝试，就如同复杂科学的出现，开始将目光从过大的天体、过小的原子而转向日常生活中如水龙头的水滴，湍流，气体，海岸线这样的难以计算的事物；或许就如痴迷于国际象棋的克劳德·香农一样，我们是不是也可以用科学的视角来严肃且深入地研究一些「很简单」的游戏，就像这篇文章一样？

这不是一件容易的事，就像 Wolfram 试图进行的，实际上是通过人类层面对游戏的思考来类比对照量子力学一样，在这篇文章的例子中，即便有强大，能将大量计算可视化的 Wolfram 语言和框架的帮助，游戏的简单规则中蕴含着的人类语言和思维难以捕捉的可能性，以及「多重计算的不可还原性」也远远足以让人意识到游戏中存在的某些惊人的事物。

游戏设计者到底创造出来的是什么？

存在于时间中的我们「只能」在一次次的重复中穿过这些复杂分支的多路图，用直觉，灵感，积累去捕捉，去做出某些棋子的决定，那四维生物是否能够一瞬间同时看到所有魔方转动的可能性呢？当我们哀叹人类棋手败于 AI，但我却觉得，人类作为如此不擅长计算的生物（所谓计算受限的实体 computationally bounded entities），居然能够在这样离散和计算化的博弈中抗衡深度神经网络多少亿万次，和多少参数的计算，这以足以令人惊奇了。

那么，当物理学家和数学家取道于游戏来阐述些什么事时，我们或许应该问：为何游戏总是被取道，游戏为何有能力，去成为这些最深奥知识的中介呢？游戏和它们，和世界的规则，秘密之间是什么关系？在这个意义上，就像是数学是对世界的抽象，而揭示出某些面向，而游戏也总是某种「揭示」，展露出了某种现实，并且成为正在发生的现实。

很多对于计算机的哲学讨论有着离散和连续/模拟和数字的对照，但在物理学的视角下，下降到足够低的层级（甚至是普朗克时间），就像 Wolfram 在文章开头所说的「物理世界在最低层次上是离散的——就像游戏和谜题一样」，而对于游戏来说，自然最终是离散亦或是连续的并非重点，重要的是游戏制作者如何有能力在不同的层面构建离散和联系的关联，并且以人类视角（Humanizing），将这些语言难以捕捉，计算不可还原的多路过程展开。

这篇文章所展示的计算分析方法，以及对现有游戏的计算性解构，或许也能直接地给游戏设计的思考带来的启发，「当我们发现多路图在某种程度上「难以解码（decode）」时，我们就会得到一个丰富的、吸引人的游戏或谜题」，而也正是一种对于游戏设计所在着手处理的事物的一次正面且直接的计算呈现，游戏设计在做什么？在某种意义上来说，便正是在调校，试验这些不可还原的多路和分支图的形态。

本文得益于 Wolfram 语言的强大计算能力，而却也只能从极简的例子出发，更无涉电子游戏，动作游戏等，不禁令人好奇，如 MOBA 游戏是否能以这种方式分析？人工智能视角下的这些多路图的空间是怎样的？游戏是什么东西「理想模型」？种种这也问题依旧引起我们的好奇，而从此文其中得以一窥的错综复杂，大概也正是游戏之难以言说的缘故吧。

Stephen Wolfram

斯蒂芬 · 沃尔夫拉姆（Stephen Wolfram）是 Mathematica，Wolfram | Alpha 和 Wolfram 语言的创始人，《一种新科学》（A New Kind of Science）的作者，Wolfram 物理计划的发起人，以及 Wolfram Research 公司的创始人和首席执行官。在四十多年的时间里，他一直是计算思维发展和应用的先驱ーー并在科学、技术和商业领域做出许多发现、发明和创新。

沃尔夫拉姆 1959 年出生于伦敦，曾就读于伊顿公学、牛津大学和加州理工学院。他在 15 岁时发表了第一篇科学论文，并在 20 岁时获得了加州理工学院的理论物理学博士学位。沃尔夫拉姆早期的科学工作主要是在高能物理学、量子场论和宇宙学方面，其中包括一些现在已经成为经典的结果。他从 1973 年开始使用计算机，迅速成为新兴科学计算领域的领导者。1979 年，他开始构建 smp - 第一个现代计算机代数系统，并于 1981 年商业化发布。

为了表彰他在物理学和计算机方面的早期工作，沃尔夫拉姆在 1981 年成为麦克阿瑟奖学金（MacArthur Fellowship）最年轻的获得者。1981 年底，他开始了一个雄心勃勃的科学新方向，旨在理解自然界复杂性的起源。他第一个关键想法是使用计算机实验来研究被称为元胞自动机（cellular automata）的简单计算机程序的行为。这让他对复杂性的起源有了一系列惊人的发现。沃尔夫拉姆发表的论文迅速产生了重大影响，为他称为复杂系统研究的新兴领域奠定了基础。

20 世纪 80 年代中期，沃尔夫拉姆继续他在复杂性方面的工作，发现了计算和自然之间的一些基本联系，并创造了诸如计算不可还原性（本篇中提及）等概念。沃尔夫拉姆的工作带来了广泛的应用，并为复杂性理论和人工生命等计划提供了主要的科学基础。沃尔夫拉姆本人用他的想法开发了一种新的随机生成系统和一种计算流体动力学的新方法——这两种方法现在都被广泛使用。

随着他在复杂系统研究方面的科学工作，沃尔夫拉姆于 1986 年创办了该领域的第一本杂志《复杂系统》（Complex Systems），并建立了其第一个研究中心。在经历了一段非常成功的学术生涯后——先是在加州理工学院，然后在普林斯顿高级研究院，最后在伊利诺斯州大学担任物理、数学和计算机科学教授——沃尔夫拉姆创立了 Wolfram Research, Inc.。

沃尔夫拉姆在 1986 年底开始开发 Mathematica。Mathematica 的第一个版本于 1988 年 6 月 23 日发布，立即被誉为计算领域的重大进步。在随后的几年里，Mathematica 的受欢迎程度迅速增长，Wolfram Research 成为软件行业的世界领导者，在技术和商业方面的卓越被广泛认可。从它最初作为一个技术计算系统开始，Mathematica 在过去的几年里在范围上急剧增长——在超过 30 年的过程中，它在许多领域和行业中负责许多重要的发明和发现，以及成为一代又一代学生教育的中心工具。

1991 年，沃尔夫拉姆开始把他的时间分配在 Mathematica 开发和科学研究之间。在 20 世纪 80 年代中期工作的基础上，现在又有了 Mathematica 作为工具，迅速取得了一系列重大的新发现。到了 20 世纪 90 年代中期，他的发现使他发展出了一个全新的概念框架，然后在 90 年代剩下的时间里，他不仅将这个框架应用于新的问题，而且还应用于物理学、生物学、计算机科学、数学和其他几个领域中许多现存的基础问题。

经过十多年高度集中的工作，沃尔夫拉姆终于在他 1200 页的《一种新科学》一书中描述了他的成就。这本书于 2002 年 5 月 14 日发行，广受好评，并立即成为畅销书。它的出版被视为开启了科学领域具有历史重要性的范式转变，每年都有新的含义出现。《一种新科学》包含或激发了许多具体的发现，包括最简单的逻辑公理系统和最简单的通用图灵机。

基于 Mathematica 和《一种新科学》的思想，沃尔夫拉姆开始了一个更雄心勃勃的项目：构建一个系统，使世界上尽可能多的知识可以立即计算，并让每个人都可以访问。Wolfram | Alpha 在 2009 年 5 月的发布被广泛认为是历史性的一步，它为计算和人工智能定义了一个新的维度——现在数百万人每天都依赖它直接或通过智能助手（如 Siri 和 Alexa）计算答案。

2014 年，沃尔夫拉姆取得了另一个突破，在 Mathematica 和 Wolfram|Alpha 的基础上创建了 Wolfram 语言。基于沃尔夫拉姆在过去三十年中开发的前所未有的深度技术栈，Wolfram 语言引入了全尺度计算语言（full-scale computational language）的新概念，它集成了大量关于计算和世界的知识，从而实现计算性描述和自动化的新水平，这可以作为大量基于计算的新领域的基础。

2020 年，在近 30 年发展的思想基础上，沃尔夫拉姆宣布在发现物理学基本理论方面取得突破，并启动了 Wolfram 物理学计划，以鼓励广泛参与这一雄心勃勃的历史性项目。

Games and Puzzles as Multicomputational Systems

June 8, 2022


日常视角下的多重计算过程
Humanizing Multicomputational Processes

多重计算（Multicomputational）是「Wolfram 物理项目」（ Wolfram Physics Project）的核心概念之一，尤其是我们对量子力学的新兴理解的核心。但是，如何才能对从一开始就很抽象的多重计算的概念有一个直观的认识呢？

我相信，一个好的方法是在熟悉的系统和情况中看到它起作用。

我在这里探讨一个似乎特别好的例子：游戏和谜题。

人们可能不会想到，像众所周知的游戏和谜题这样的日常事物会与量子力学这样的形式化理论有任何联系。但是多重计算的观点提供了一个关联。事实上，我们可以把存在「有趣的」游戏和谜题的这种恰好的可能性本身，与多重计算的一个核心现象联系起来，即多重计算的不可还原性（multicomputational irreducibility）。

（译注：「多重计算的不可还原性」这个翻译中的「还原」含义类似与「还原论」中的「还原」，有将复杂的事物归结到简单事物的含义）

在一个普通的计算系统中，系统的每个状态都有一个唯一的后续状态（successor），而且最终有一个单一的时间线来定义一个计算过程。但在多重计算系统中，关键就在于每个状态可以有多个后续状态——追踪它们的行为定义了一个由时间线程的分支和合并组成的一个完整的多路图（multiway graph）。而关键就在于，这与人们如何思考典型的游戏和谜题直接相关。

给定某个游戏或谜题的一个特定状态，玩家通常必须决定下一步该做什么。他们通常有很多选择可以做，这个时候多重计算的概念就出现了。在一次特定的游戏过程（实例 instance）中，他们会做出一个特定的选择。而多重计算范式（paradigm）的关键，是全局地看待所有可能选择的结果——并产生一个代表这些选择的多路图（Multiway Graph）。

为游戏和谜题构造这样的多路图的做法实际上已经存在了 100 多年了——通常被叫做「游戏图（game graphs）」 。但随着多重计算范式的出现，现在有一些更一般的概念可以应用于这些结构。反过来，理解这些结构与游戏和谜题的关系可以提供关于多路图新层次的直观和熟悉的理解。

我在这里的具体目标是，使用我们一直在发展的研究多重计算系统的一般方法，来足够系统性地研究一系列众所周知的游戏和谜题。就像是在与日常事物相关的研究中通常会出现的那样，我们会遭遇各种具体细节。虽然这些细节可能不会立即被关联到更大尺度的讨论，但对于为我们提供实际游戏和谜题的现实且可联系的画面来说，它们是很重要的，这也能使我们与多重计算的联系有了一个坚实的基础。

值得一提的是，将游戏和谜题与物理学联系起来的可能性，如果没有我们的「物理学计划」（Wolfram Physics Project，校注：项目的官方文章中的描述：「我认为我们已经找到了一条通往物理学基础理论的道路」），就基本上很难理解。

因为游戏和谜题通常在某种最根本层面上是离散的——特别是在它们涉及离散的可能性分支的方面。而如果我们假设物理学从根本上是连续的，那么就没有理由期待它与游戏和谜题会有联系。但我们的「物理学计划」的一个关键想法是，物理世界在最低层次上是离散的——就像游戏和谜题一样。并且更重要的是，我们的「物理学计划」认为，物理学就像游戏和谜题一样，有离散的可能性可探索。

我在这里讨论的每一个游戏和谜题，在结构和操作（operation）上，一开始都可能显得相当不同。但我们将看到的是，当以一种多重计算的视角来看时，在我们不同的例子中，存在着显著的、几乎是千篇一律的统一性（uniformity）。在文本结尾的部分，我会开始讨论各种重要的多重计算现象如何在游戏和谜题的背景中起作用，在此之前我不会过多地评论这些现象的意义。我也会在最后讨论用简单直接的人类语言对多重计算进行概念化是何等困难——而正是它从根本上导致了游戏和谜题的迷人特性。

多重计算视角下的推论和阐释 Multicomputational Implications & Interpretation

我们已经考察了许多游戏和谜题的例子。在每一个例子中，我们都探索了囊括了整个可能行为谱系的多路图。那么，我们的结论是什么呢？

最明显的一点是，如果游戏和谜题在我们看来是困难的——或者说是「有趣的」——它在某种程度上为多路图的显著复杂性所反映。或者，换句话说，当我们发现多路图在某种程度上「难以解码（decode）」时，我们就会得到一个丰富的、吸引人的游戏或谜题。

在玩一个游戏的任何特定实例中，我们基本上是沿着一条特定的路径（与物理学相类似，我们可以称之为「时间路径（timelike path）」）穿过游戏的多路图（或「游戏图」）。并且在某种程度上，我们可能只是做了一个全局性的声明，即游戏图代表了所有这样的路径。

但多重计算范式（Multicomputational paradigm）所建议的是，我们还可以有效地做出更多的局部声明。特别是，在沿着一条时间路径的每一步，我们可以在多路图中「横断地（transversally）」观察，并看到「瞬时分支图」，它代表了我们的路径与「邻近路径」的「纠缠（entanglement）」。

从而，某种意义上说，弄清「下一步该做什么」就是决定在分支空间中「朝什么方向」走。而游戏的困难之处在于，我们无法轻易预知我们「穿越分支空间」时发生了什么。这里有一个与计算的不可还原性（computational Irreducibility）概念的某种类比。沿着一些时间路径从一个状态到另一个状态，计算的不可还原性意味着，即使我们可能知道根本的规则，我们也不能轻易地预测其结果——因为这可能需要不可减少的计算量来计算出许多步骤之后的结果。

预测「穿越分支空间」是一个相关的、但稍有不同的现象，人们可以将其描述为「多重计算的不可还原性（multicomputational irreducibility）」。这不是关于计算出一个特定路径的困难，而是关于看到许多纠缠的路径如何相互作用的困难。

当一个人在玩游戏时，通常会谈论「能往前看到多少步」。而在我们这里，这基本上是在问我们可以轻易获知能在分支空间里走多远。作为计算上受约束的实体（computationally bounded entities），我们在分支空间有一定的「触达范围」。如果这个范围不足以达到类似「获胜点」的地方，那么这个游戏对我们来说就是「困难的」。

不过，这里还有一个问题。在一个游戏中「获胜」的因素通常是在多路图中达到一些特定的地方或区域。但这些地方或区域的定义通常是一些计算上在约束范围内的东西（「只要看看是否有一行 X」，等等）。这是对系统的某种「观察」，它只是提取了完整状态的一个特定的（计算约束内）采样。然后，关键在于，这个采样并没有设法去「解码多重计算的不可还原性」。

这里有一个与热力学的类比。在热力学中，我们感知到「热」和「熵增加」的事实是这样的：我们的（粗粒度的）度量不能「解码」导致系统中产生的特定状态的不可还原的过程。同样，我们认为「很难弄清楚如何赢得一场游戏」的事实是这样一个结果，即我们的获胜判断标准不能去「观察游戏的内部」和「解码正在发生的事」，直到说它实际上成为只是选择一个特定的、简单径直的路径。相反，它是一个去经历玩游戏的多重计算不可还原的过程的问题，并且相对于对胜利的观察，实际上是「看看它会落在什么位置（seeing where it lands）」。

这里也有一个与量子力学的类比。追溯玩一个游戏的许多可能路径，就像追寻量子力学中的许多历史线程（threads），而获胜的标准就像一个选择某些线程的量子度量。在我们的「物理学计划」中，我们想象我们作为观察者是在分支空间中延伸的，通过我们对自己的单一经验线程的信念，将不同的历史线程「编织在一起」。在游戏中，我们对单一经验线的信念的类比，大概就是「重要的是谁赢谁输；游戏具体是怎么玩的并不重要」。

为了与量子力学做一个更接近的类比，我们可以开始考虑将「多路游玩」的不同部分结合起来，并试图为这些部分如何结合起来制定一套「微积分学」。

我们在这里讨论的游戏在某种意义上都是纯粹的「技巧游戏」。但在也有运气因素的游戏中，我们可以认为这导致了多路图中的单一路径「模糊化（fuzz out）」为一束路径，以及本来是分支空间中的一个点变成了整个扩展区域。

在研究不同的具体游戏和谜题时，我们经常不得不去研究一些相当简化的案例，以便得到规模可控的多路图。但是，如果我们研究非常大的多路图，是否会有整体的规律性涌现？对于游戏图来说，是否存在某种潜在的「连续极限（continuum limit）」？

几乎不可避免的是，如果我们看得「足够详细」，我们就会看到各种多重计算的不可还原性在发挥作用。但在我们的「物理学计划」中，甚至在一般的多重计算范式中，一个关键的问题是，相关的观察者并没有看到那个层次的细节。就像热力学或气体定律从底层分子动力学中的「涌现（emergence ）」一样，底层计算的不可还原性的存在，不可避免地导致观察者所能感知的简单定律。

那么，对于一个游戏来说，「观察者」的类比是什么呢？至少在某些方面，它可以被认为是「获胜」的判断标准。那么现在问题来了：如果我们只看这些标准，我们能不能推导出「物理定律」的类似物，而不敏感于其下的所有多重计算的不可还原的细节？

关于这一点，还有很多东西需要弄清楚，但也许可以从一个地方开始，看看各种游戏中的分支空间和多路图的大规模结构。在许多不同的游戏中，一个基本的印象是，虽然分支图的特征可能在游戏的「不同阶段」之间发生变化，但在单个分支图中，往往有某种统一性。如果我们看一下细节，可能有很多多重计算的不可还原性。但在某种「可感知的水平」上，图的不同部分可能看起来很相似。这表明，即使已经采取了相当不同的行动，将人们带到由分支图定义的「游戏空间」的相当不同部分，「游戏的局部印象」在某一特定阶段往往是相似的，。

但是，虽然分支图的不同部分之间可能存在相似性，但我们看到的是，在一些游戏和谜题中，分支图会分成多个不相连的区域。这反映了游戏中存在着不同的「守恒区（conserved sectors）」——玩家可以进入的游戏空间区域，但随后会被卡住（至少在一定时间内），就像在时空中事件视界（event horizons，校注：德国天文学家卡尔·史瓦西提出的涉及黑洞的概念，一旦光线或物质越过事件视界，就永远无法逃脱了）可以阻止物理空间的不同区域之间的传送。

我们在一些游戏和谜题中注意到的另一个（相关的）现象是多路图中的大「洞」：在图中两点之间有多条「遥远」的路径。当多路图是密集连接的时候，通常总是有办法通过附近的路径改道来 「修复任何错误」。但是，当有一个洞时，这就表明人们最终会「致力于（committed）」某个行动的进程而不是另一个，而且要经过许多步骤才有可能到达与另一个行动进程所能到达的相同的地方。

如果我们假设在某个层面上，我们在多路图中最终「观察」到的是与评估输赢相对应的那种粗粒度，那么我们将不可避免地处理一个可能路径的分布情况。在没有「洞」的情况下，这些路径可能很接近，而且看起来很相似。但是当有洞的时候，可能会有相距甚远的不同的路径。而「属于相同分布部分」的遥远路径可能被认为是类似于量子叠加效应的事实。

游戏中是否有类似于广义相对论和路径积分（path integral）的概念？为了清楚地表述这个问题，我们必须更仔细地定义「游戏空间」的特征。很可能会有因果图（causal graph）的类似物。也很可能游戏空间中也会有一个类似能量的概念，与游戏空间中不同地方的「活动密度」相关。

那么，引力现象的类似物将是这样的：最好的游戏的游玩方式（即通过游戏图的测地路径）将倾向于被高活动密度的存在所偏转。换句话说，如果一个游戏处于某种状态时有很多事要做，那么好的游戏游玩将倾向于「被拉向那个状态」。在某种程度上，这并不令人惊讶：当游戏图中存在高密度的活动时，往往会有更多关于做什么的选择，因此，如果一个玩家经过那里，就更有可能 「玩出一场精彩的游戏」。

到目前为止，我们还没有明确地谈论游戏的策略。但在我们的多重计算框架中，策略有一个相当明确的解释：它是可能规则空间（rulial space）中的一个地方，在那里，人们实际上是假设了一套关于如何构建多路图的规则。换句话说，给定一个策略，人们就会在多路图中选择一些边（或者在相关的多路因果图中选择一些可能的事件），而放弃其他的边。

一般来说，谈论「可能策略的空间」可能很困难，因为这就像谈论「可能程序的空间」。但这恰恰是可能规则空间（rulial space）让我们谈论的东西。「策略空间」到底有什么样的「几何结构」，将取决于我们如何选择协调可能规则空间。但是，再一次，通过仅仅只看类似于博弈论中讨论的那种东西，将倾向于实现某种程度的粗放（coarse-graining）——在这种程度上，我们可以预期所有各种标准的「结构化」的博弈论结果将普遍成立。

（译注：Rulial space 是 Wolfram 自创的一个术语，意指所有可能的规则以及这些规则的所有应用方式所组成的空间。比如，从符号 A 开始应用符号替换规则{A → AB, BB → A}，可以用下面的多路图表示这个规则所有可能的应用方式：

（这个图只画出了前几步，完整的图应该是无限的）

假设只有 A、B 两个符号，只考虑长度最多为 2 的符号串，那么所有这样的可能的替换规则有

按照上面的方式画出所有这些替换规则对应的多路图，并把这些多路图合并成一个图，就构成了这个有限语境下的 Rulial space。

现在想象我们考虑的不仅仅是上面这些符号替换规则，而是宇宙中所有可能的规则，这个巨大的 Rulial Space 可以认为包含了一切”可计算的事物（everything that is computationally possible.）“。推荐阅读：https://writings.stephenwolfram.com/2021/11/the-concept-of-the-ruliad/ ）

个人笔记 Personal Notes

即使在小时候，我也从未特别喜欢玩游戏或做拼图。而这也许是我太像个科学家的一个标志。因为只是选出特定的棋步对我来说总是显得太武断任意了。为了引起我的兴趣，我需要一个更大的图景，更加前后一致的认知叙事。

而现在，从某种意义上说，这正是我在这里讨论的对游戏和谜题的多重计算方法带给我们的东西。是的，能够思考做出特定的动作是非常「人类视角化（humanizing）」的。但是，多重计算方法立即给人了一种连贯的全局观，至少对我来说，理智上更令人满意。

我在这里讨论的探索可以被认为是源于《一种新的科学》中的一个注释。在《一种新的科学》的第五章中，我有一节首次介绍了多路系统。在那一节的最后一个注释中，我讨论了「游戏系统」。

我在 20 世纪 90 年代做了这方面的研究——事实上，我现在发现 1998 年的一本关于井字棋的文件，其中得出了一些相同的结果

其中还有一个看起来很耐人寻味的关于井字棋的图表：

但在那个时候，我并没有从我生成的这些游戏相关的图中得出什么结论；它们只是显得庞大而复杂。20 年过去了，我没有再多想这个问题。但后来在 2017 年，我的儿子克里斯托弗（https://christopherwolfram.com/）在玩一个叫《Rush Hour》的桌游。

也许是家族倾向的表现，他决定构建其游戏图——得出了对我来说似乎是非常令人惊讶的结果。

当时我并没有试图去理解这里的结构，但我还是把它「归档」了，作为游戏图可以有「可见的大规模结构」的证据。

几年后——2019 年底——我们的物理项目正在进行中，我们已经意识到，量子力学和多路图之间存在着深刻的关系。量子力学一直看起来是神秘的东西——纯数学形式主义的抽象结果。但是，看到与多路系统的联系，开始暗示人们实际上能够「理解量子力学」，因为它可以从一些具体的基础结构中「机制地产生」。

我开始思考如何在一个直观的层面上解释量子力学。为此，我需要一个熟悉的类比：可以与多路系统联系起来的日常事物。我立即想到了游戏。2020 年 9 月，我决定考察一下游戏，以更详细地探索这个类比。我很快就分析了井字游戏和尼姆游戏，以及简单的滑动块谜题和汉诺塔。但我想探索更多的游戏和谜题。而且我还有其他项目要做，所以游戏和谜题的多重计算分析被搁置了。

今年早些时候，汉诺塔又出现了，当时我把它作为一个生成类似证明的多路图的例子，与我对元数学的物理化研究有关。最后，几周前我决定是时候写下我到目前为止所知道的关于游戏和谜题的东西了——并产生了这里的东西。

致谢 Thanks

感谢 Brad Klee 和 Ed Pegg 在本文给出的分析的最后阶段提供的各种帮助——以及 Christopher Wolfram 在 2017 年的灵感和 2020 年的帮助。

落日间是一个试图回答「何为游戏」与「游戏何为」的数字人文实验室，我们希望探索一种新的扩展但具体的游戏概念，面对当今游玩化的世界并发掘电子游戏的可能形态。我们正在创作帮助我们理解游戏/电子游戏的文字，音频节目，视频，以及电子游戏（xpaidia.com）。

title: 本周 Steam 值得关注的游戏 11.16 - 11.22（三）
author: 游戏发现
text:
第二部分
注： 本系列文章的信息主要整合自 Steam 与 SteamDB 的即将发售列表，由于 Steam 支持手动输入日期及发售、同步不及时等原因，本列表可能会遗漏收录一些作品的发售信息。如果本周有您的作品或您喜欢的作品未被列出，欢迎直接评论补充链接～～
Arctic Grave
关键字： 心理恐怖、冒险、步行模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/19（暂无中文）
在这款恐怖游戏中，揭开北极货运前哨站失踪船员之谜。眺望冰封的大海，深入设施深处，收集物品，并通过每件物品发现新的路径，从而揭开这里真正发生的事情。但请小心，因为这里可能还有其他东西与你同在。
Swarmbreaker
关键字： 塔防、增量
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
《Swarmbreaker》是一款增量式塔防游戏。你必须抵御庞大的异星虫群活体狂潮，保卫你的基地。建造防御工事阻断它们的路线，部署重型武器，升级你的武库，彻底击溃虫群！
Highschool J
关键字： 心理恐怖、冒险、视觉小说
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
雪井过着平淡的生活，肩负着债务，身边只有寥寥数位好友，以及从不与任何人分享的诗篇。直到那名转学生走进教室。因为有些存在，你根本无法抗拒。你只能选择臣服。
Marque & Reprisal
关键字： 航海、模拟、类 Rogue、生存
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
探索、贸易、捕鱼、捕鲸、殖民、战斗、劫掠、生存。你是一名生活在 1522 年的船长，在这款带有 Roguelike 元素的历史航海沙盒模拟游戏中，整个世界都等待你去发现。
托托的奇幻之旅（Toto's Journey）
关键字： 狗、冒险、探索、解谜
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
《托托之旅》是一款受《绿野仙踪》世界启发的温馨冒险游戏。你将扮演勇敢的小狗托托，在一场神秘的龙卷风后迷失于魔法世界。探索被施了魔法的土地，遇见奇特的生物，并在寻找回家之路的过程中解开环境谜题。
红铃的恸哭（The Red Bells Lament）
关键字： 冒险、视觉小说、恋爱模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
某日，一封来自无名者的信， 将她引向一座神秘的庄园。 猎人与王国的骑士齐聚，迎接来自王国的密令： 「组建狩猎队，进攻吸血鬼的世界——《纽克斯》！」 这是一场关乎世界命运的赌局， 棋局已开，谁是棋子，谁能主宰未来？
MUV-LUV 少女庭园 Mellow Days（MUV-LUV GIRLS GARDEN Mellow Days）
关键字： 实用工具、挂机游戏
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
《MUV-LUV 少女庭园 Mellow Days》是一款专注陪伴冒险游戏，让你与桃园梅露共享一段时光，一起完成每天的任务。 按照自己的喜好设置番茄钟、ToDo 清单、日历、音乐和环境音。随着共同努力的时间不断累积，你与梅露的故事也会一点点展开。
纸牌巫: 魔女决战（Witch the Showdown）
关键字： 卡牌战斗、动作
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）EA
Parry × 卡组构筑 × Boss Rush 的高难度“魂系”动作游戏！ 纸牌巫魔女决战是一款以 仅与 Boss 战斗 为核心玩法的高难度 Parry 动作游戏。 玩家需要通过 精准的 Parry 积累魔力（Mana），并在 实时战斗中使用卡牌进行攻击，将 高强度操作 与 策略性卡组构筑相结合，带来极具挑战性的战斗体验。
相信直觉（Trust Your Gut）
关键字： 牌组构建式类 Rogue、赌博、心理
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
一款多球轮盘轻度 Rogue 游戏。多球齐转，用 100+ 种纪念品与 50 种花式球改写轮盘：添加颜色、改动数字、调整赔率、叠加倍率。你正被困在一档扭曲的电视直播节目里，木偶主持人咧嘴狞笑。达不到他定下的目标，节目就让你提前杀青。
Flick
关键字： 心理恐怖
发行日期： 2026/11/19（暂无中文）
只需轻轻一拨开关，现实就在你眼前翻转，把你拽入光怪陆离的世界，去揭开家族扭曲的过往。在这款心理恐怖游戏中，前进离不开光，光却也会召唤出最骇人的梦魇，你必须在两者之间小心拿捏。
Lord of Undead
关键字： 开放世界生存制作、动作角色扮演
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）EA
在这款阴暗的 RPG 中扮演黑暗领主，摧毁山上的城堡。收集灵魂，召唤亡灵军队，亵渎这片广阔开放世界的土地并建立你的基地。
Save the Forest
关键字： 轻度 Rogue、回合制战术、角色扮演
发行日期： 2026/11/19（暂无中文）
《Save the Forest》是一款回合制战术 Roguelite 游戏，你将带领一支村民小队，踏上击败那股——不得不承认确实挺傻的——邪恶势力的征程，这股邪恶势力已经腐蚀了整片森林。结合单位升级、精准的战术布阵，以及来自意想不到的森林居民们的帮助，一起踏上这场冒险吧！
我的梦想家（Tiny Dwellings）
关键字： 建造、设计与插画、休闲
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
在《我的梦想家》里打造你的梦中情屋吧！这里没有任务与倒计时，只有纯粹的治愈和放松。超过 1000 种精美部件任你挑选，从零开始布置专属于你的小屋与庭院。放慢脚步，伴随着慵懒的 Lo-fi 音乐，沉浸在柔软的光影中，感受昼夜交替与晴雨变化。快来建造你的梦想小窝，享受一段宁静的悠闲时光吧！
失明恐惧症（Blind Phobia）
关键字： 探索、步行模拟、心理恐怖
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
你失明了，并且被困在了一个无限循环的医院走廊里。你需要利用导盲杖和其他感官来寻找异常，质疑幻觉，找到逃生之路。
元素尾巴（ELEMENTAIL）
关键字： 卡牌战斗、类 Rogue
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
“抽牌、吞噬、攻击!” 与可爱的动物魔法师一起，策略性地组合水·火·雷三种元素卡牌的休闲卡组构筑类 Roguelike 游戏—《Elementail》。收集并强化 150 种宝物，探索孔雀工匠的工作坊，拯救被污染的世界吧!
爪爪奶茶店（Paw's Boba Shop）
关键字： 烹饪、制作、商店管理
发行日期： 2026/11/19（ 中文支持 ）
爪爪奶茶店是一个自由调配奶茶，为不同的可爱动物客人提供饮品的奶茶店模拟经营游戏。你可以尝试混合基底，手捣水果、榨果汁、做冰沙，用糖果、饼干等装饰饮品。没有倒计时和压力，可以按任意节奏游玩。
Tún
关键字： 休闲、农场模拟、解谜
发行日期： 2026/11/19（暂无中文）
《Tún》是一款轻松惬意的解谜游戏，玩家可以按照自己的节奏打理花园。完成任务、扩建花园、随心所欲地装饰，还可以收养猫咪。没有游戏结束一说，也不会让人感到压力过大。
No More Seats
关键字： 心理恐怖、自选历险体验
发行日期： 2026/11/19（暂无中文）
一部紧张刺激的第一人称恐怖惊悚片，讲述了一座城市的疏散故事。在公交车站对乘客进行测试，核实他们的说法，并决定谁能登上最后一班公交车——因为车厢里只要藏着一名聆听者，就意味着所有人将面临灭顶之灾。
Crack In The Dark
关键字： 探索、冒险、动作
发行日期： 2026/11/19（暂无中文）EA
《Crack in the Dark》是一款洞穴探索游戏，你需要依靠声音来“看见”世界。绘制自己的地图，以免在广阔的洞穴系统中迷失，并依靠你的鞭子进行战斗、移动与导航。
第四部分
最后一部分周五下午送上！

只需轻轻一拨开关，现实就在你眼前翻转，把你拽入光怪陆离的世界，去揭开家族扭曲的过往。在这款心理恐怖游戏中，前进离不开光，光却也会召唤出最骇人的梦魇，你必须在两者之间小心拿捏。

Lord of Undead

发行日期：2026/11/19（中文支持）EA

在这款阴暗的 RPG 中扮演黑暗领主，摧毁山上的城堡。收集灵魂，召唤亡灵军队，亵渎这片广阔开放世界的土地并建立你的基地。

Save the Forest

关键字：轻度 Rogue、回合制战术、角色扮演

发行日期：2026/11/19（暂无中文）

《Save the Forest》是一款回合制战术 Roguelite 游戏，你将带领一支村民小队，踏上击败那股——不得不承认确实挺傻的——邪恶势力的征程，这股邪恶势力已经腐蚀了整片森林。结合单位升级、精准的战术布阵，以及来自意想不到的森林居民们的帮助，一起踏上这场冒险吧！

我的梦想家（Tiny Dwellings）

发行日期：2026/11/19（中文支持）

在《我的梦想家》里打造你的梦中情屋吧！这里没有任务与倒计时，只有纯粹的治愈和放松。超过 1000 种精美部件任你挑选，从零开始布置专属于你的小屋与庭院。放慢脚步，伴随着慵懒的 Lo-fi 音乐，沉浸在柔软的光影中，感受昼夜交替与晴雨变化。快来建造你的梦想小窝，享受一段宁静的悠闲时光吧！

失明恐惧症（Blind Phobia）

关键字：探索、步行模拟、心理恐怖

发行日期：2026/11/19（中文支持）

你失明了，并且被困在了一个无限循环的医院走廊里。你需要利用导盲杖和其他感官来寻找异常，质疑幻觉，找到逃生之路。

元素尾巴（ELEMENTAIL）

关键字：卡牌战斗、类 Rogue

发行日期：2026/11/19（中文支持）

“抽牌、吞噬、攻击!” 与可爱的动物魔法师一起，策略性地组合水·火·雷三种元素卡牌的休闲卡组构筑类 Roguelike 游戏—《Elementail》。收集并强化 150 种宝物，探索孔雀工匠的工作坊，拯救被污染的世界吧!

爪爪奶茶店（Paw's Boba Shop）

关键字：烹饪、制作、商店管理

发行日期：2026/11/19（中文支持）

爪爪奶茶店是一个自由调配奶茶，为不同的可爱动物客人提供饮品的奶茶店模拟经营游戏。你可以尝试混合基底，手捣水果、榨果汁、做冰沙，用糖果、饼干等装饰饮品。没有倒计时和压力，可以按任意节奏游玩。

《Tún》是一款轻松惬意的解谜游戏，玩家可以按照自己的节奏打理花园。完成任务、扩建花园、随心所欲地装饰，还可以收养猫咪。没有游戏结束一说，也不会让人感到压力过大。

No More Seats

关键字：心理恐怖、自选历险体验

发行日期：2026/11/19（暂无中文）

一部紧张刺激的第一人称恐怖惊悚片，讲述了一座城市的疏散故事。在公交车站对乘客进行测试，核实他们的说法，并决定谁能登上最后一班公交车——因为车厢里只要藏着一名聆听者，就意味着所有人将面临灭顶之灾。

title: 互动影游出现新黑马！十多位女主、产品三天销量破5万套
excerpt: 早在2024年7月，深圳一支小团队爆米互动做了款真人影游，名字叫《重生了还要我谈恋爱》，讲的是一个年轻人重生后与六位女性相识的故事。两年后，在AI短剧和互动剧大热的当下，这批主创带着新的真人产品《重生2我独自…
text:
早在2024年7月，深圳一支小团队爆米互动做了款真人影游，名字叫《重生了还要我谈恋爱》，讲的是一个年轻人重生后与六位女性相识的故事。主创用了五个月完成开发，试着往恋爱剧情中加入道具收集、解谜和QTE战斗，遗憾的是市场反响平淡。
两年后，在AI短剧和互动剧大热的当下，这批主创带着新的真人产品《重生2我独自逆袭》回到了Steam。
前作中的白芙和小恋都在，可发展感情的角色增加到十余位，商店页仍把真人恋爱放在显眼位置。但在游戏里，主角有了一份具体日程：白天上班，下班后可以找兼职，或者回家陪妹妹。一段剧情能否发生，取决于玩家前几天把时间花在了哪里。
11月13日，《重生2》以46.4元的国区首发价上线。制作组随后宣布，游戏在Steam发售三天销量突破5万套，对应的估算流水在200万人民币左右。
得益于KOL和头部主播的宣发，游戏同时在线峰值一度冲到6215人，近两千条评测中约96%为好评。
兔娘进行了《重生2》的直播
如今距离《完蛋！我被美女包围了！》走红正好三年。
这段时间里，国产真人影游已经拍过情感骗局，也拍出了卖到数百万套的宫廷剧。《重生2》提供了另一个观察角度：即使沿用熟悉的都市恋爱题材，改变玩家参与故事的方式，也能做出两款体验颇为不同的产品。
下班以后，玩家接手主角的生活
《重生2》给主角设定了一个典型的爽剧目标：从城中村的出租屋起步，最后有机会成为上市公司CEO。
开场时，主角还是个因缺勤险些丢掉工作的设计师，房租已经逾期，正在复读的妹妹也需要补习费。这个开局除了交代人物处境，还有一个设计上的好处：地图刚开放，玩家就知道自己为什么需要赚钱。
下班后的自由活动是游戏的重心。去理发店兼职能挣一笔外快，办健身卡要花钱，但练出来的属性会影响之后的打斗。游戏每天只给有限的行动力，几件单看都值得做的事，放在同一个晚上就有了冲突。
照顾妹妹这条支线，更容易看出这套设计与普通对话选项的区别。
玩家可以给她50元零花钱，也可以坐下来辅导功课。后者不花钱，但要消耗两个行动点，主角的智力还得达到20。两种做法都符合哥哥的身份，但这个晚上他能怎么做，要看他手里还剩多少钱，此前几天又是怎么过的。
相比之前的纯PPT影游，这算是在交互性上的进步。
比如同样是50元，你可以拿去买刮刮乐，也可以到公园里从一个兜售武功秘籍的乞丐手里买下《如来神掌》。从背包里读完秘籍，下次回到公园，地图上就多了一项练掌的活动。一次偶遇，由此改变了往后几天的日程。
爆米互动还在试玩期间调整过战斗设计，让按键反应不够快的玩家有机会靠此前的角色养成通过挑战。这也让玩家愿意花时间练拳：等到实拍的打斗戏开始，前几天在地图上做的事，会反映到剧情走向上。
在叙事层面，制作组也给偏爱恋爱剧情的老玩家留了余地。只要专注攻略喜欢的角色，同样能走到好结局。
毕竟如果每段感情戏前面都横着一道数值门槛，养成很快就会变成看下一集的负担。《重生2》把较多可供钻研的内容留在自由行动时段，想追角色的人可以沿着故事走，对逆袭过程更有兴趣的人，则有理由多跑几次地图。
另外，相比竞品，游戏在视觉表现上的尺度是非常激进的。这为产品提供了更强的吸量钩子，但确实也容易引起争议，算是一把双刃剑。
从选择恋爱对象，到判断对方来意
在2023年的《完蛋！我被美女包围了！》里，玩家扮演顾易，以第一人称和六位女性相识。几乎不需要玩法教学，人物一出场，玩家就能判断自己对谁更有好感。直播又放大了这种体验，即使没有亲自操作，观众也能替顾易拿主意。
最先被同行学走的，自然是这个清晰的恋爱设定。
2024年3月，《美女，请别影响我学习》把舞台搬进女子大学，让主角成为全校唯一的男生。《重生》第一部也诞生在这个时期：重生是故事的入口，恋爱仍然是玩家进入游戏时最明确的期待。
到了2025年，《情感反诈模拟器》保留了异性主动接近主角的情境，却让玩家扮演一个受过骗、试图打入诈骗团伙的人。同样一句示好，放在顾易耳边，玩家考虑的是如何回应；到了这里，玩家得判断对方为何偏偏在这个时候接近自己。
这某种程度上反映了恋爱影游赛道的题材变迁，以及受众群体心态的转折。
宫廷剧和警匪片，也找到了各自的玩法
如果把视野放大到整个互动剧赛道，会发现行业正在进行广度和深度的同步拓展。
《隐形守护者》团队New One Studio做《盛世天下》，抓住了宫廷剧观众一种由来已久的乐趣——判断角色究竟在哪一步说错了话。
《媚娘篇》里，玩家扮演初入宫廷的伍元照。姨母杨舒妃端来桂花羹时，决定命运的往往是此前几句应对。玩家反复读档，自然会重新留意初看时忽略的语气和措辞。后来，喝过几碗桂花羹成了玩家交流进度的暗号，一场失败戏也有了反复观看的价值。
今年6月，《盛世天下：女帝篇》上线12天，全平台销量突破200万套。到9月，制作人公布，上下两篇累计销量超过600万套。
就连《完蛋》的开发团队小有内容，今年也拍起了港式卧底故事。在粤语原声的《对不起，我是警察》里，玩家要潜入回归前的香港黑帮。团队只设了一个真正的结局，沿途如何在警察的职责与眼前的兄弟情义之间周旋，仍然有足够的戏留给玩家。
在罗斯基看来，相比上面这些大制作，《重生2》给这三年补上的，其实是题材之外的另一条线索。
毕竟过去大家谈互动影游，基本都在说影像的部分，鲜少有人关注“互动”本身。而《重生2》做的事非常日常，还把一部分决定权提前交给玩家，并影响下一场戏如何展开。
这种独一无二的体验和记忆，或许才是《重生2》取得商业成绩的核心。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 首周60万销量+千万流水：做了三年游戏后，这个8人团队终于靠“上课偷吃”翻了身
excerpt: 那么在这么短的时间里，他们是怎样从一段大家都懂的生活经验里，找到了一个适合反复游玩的点子呢？黄泉接受采访时透露过一个细节：试玩期间，有玩家建议开放教室后门，再加入下蹲动作，让学生能绕到走廊，悄悄移动到教室前方…
text:
老师转过身，开始在黑板上写字；你赶紧低头，从课桌里掏出零食。吃到一半，身旁突然安静下来。等你抬起头，老师已经站在面前——这段不少人都熟悉的经历，如今成了一款Steam游戏的核心乐趣。
11月17日，《我带过的最差一届》发布首周成绩：销量突破60万份。SteamDB数据显示，游戏最高同时在线人数达到46,566人，好评率约87%，维持在“特别好评”。
VGI估算，游戏首周流水已突破140万美元（约合1000万人民币），且还在快速增长。
它的开发团队顽核社只有8个人。从玩法验证到试玩版上线，前后只用了约一个月。那么在这么短的时间里，他们是怎样从一段大家都懂的生活经验里，找到了一个适合反复游玩的点子呢？
学生负责装老实，老师负责找破绽
《我带过的最差一届》最多支持8人联机。标准玩法中，1人扮演老师，其余玩家扮演学生，混在几十名NPC同学之间。学生要找机会偷吃零食、玩手机，完成各种捣乱任务。老师则在人群中寻找破绽，抓出真正的玩家。
在实际体验里，学生不能一直安静坐着。想推进任务，就得冒险搞小动作；低头偷吃时，视野又会受到限制，只能留意脚步声和板书声，猜测老师现在在哪里。多吃两口，可能更接近目标，也可能来不及收手。
老师同样无法毫无顾忌地四处抓人。体力不足时，需要回到黑板前写字恢复。视线一转过去，台下就有了发挥空间。等老师再次回头，一屋子学生已经恢复端坐，仿佛什么都没发生。
所以双方争夺的，是那几秒钟的空当。
抓捕之外，队友还能寻找机会救人。烟雾和墨水等道具可以制造混乱，老师则能借助摄像头、雷达搜查。一群熟人挤进房间后，互相掩护、临时甩锅或者看朋友被抓，都可能成为一局里最让人记得住的片段。
这个设计巧妙的地方，在于题材直接解释了玩法。甚至连名字都省下了一段介绍：“你们是我带过的最差一届”，许多人看到这句话，脑海里就已经有声音了。
一个短视频热点，长成了多人游戏
游戏的灵感，确实来自现实中的“偷吃大赛”。团队负责人黄泉在采访中透露，团队平时会关注短视频热点。
看到成年人重新坐进模拟教室，趁扮演老师的工作人员转身时偷吃，他们判断这个场景可以做成游戏。因为这里面的笑点甚至不需要等到抓捕成功，仅仅是有人手忙脚乱地藏东西，就足以让人继续看下去。
到了游戏里，这种冲突有了更多变数。真人学生藏在NPC中，老师需要辨认；朋友可以互相配合，也可能添乱；不同道具又让现场不断失控。同一个教室，换了一群人，便可能发生另一套故事。
更有意思的是，传播还会反过来影响开发。
黄泉接受采访时透露过一个细节：试玩期间，有玩家建议开放教室后门，再加入下蹲动作，让学生能绕到走廊，悄悄移动到教室前方。团队很快采纳，随后短视频平台上出现了更多蹲行、趴地躲避老师的片段。
这给小团队的发行策略提供了启发：观察社区反馈时，除了寻找哪里不好玩，也可以留意玩家想在游戏里做出什么行为。那些让人跃跃欲试的动作，往往同时具备游玩和传播价值。
四周做出Demo之前，他们已经做了多年游戏
顽核社此前的经历，非常曲折。
团队于2021年底成立。早期作品《地心归途》研发超过三年，最终卖出十多万份。据黄泉透露，这笔收入主要够给团队补发一些工资，后续项目又没能顺利拿到投资。继续投入生存建造项目，已经超出了当时团队的资金承受范围。
于是他们开始寻找体量更小、验证更快的方向，多人派对游戏进入了视野。
在《最差一届》之前，团队还尝试过需要用声音驱赶鸭子的《胡闹赶鸭》，以及一个后来暂时搁置的盗墓题材项目。转型并没有立即带来爆款，但他们逐渐熟悉了这种产品的开发节奏。
《最差一届》从玩法验证到Demo上线，大约花了一个月。这段时间的背后，是团队此前积累的研发能力，也是对项目规模的一次重新选择。
大型内容项目需要不断投入，市场反馈却可能来得很晚。围绕清晰互动规则展开的多人游戏，可以更早把核心体验交给玩家，再决定如何继续投入。队友之间产生的意外，也为重复游玩提供了大量变化。
《最差一届》恰好赶上了适合自己的节奏。游戏Demo在10月Steam新品节获得玩家数榜第一，累计试玩人数超过60万。11月10日，正式版紧接着发售，由2P Games与Elegoose Games联合发行，把试玩阶段的关注转化为付费购买。
一路看下来，所谓的“快”，既包括开发速度，也包括识别题材和承接热度的速度。
热闹之后，还要让朋友愿意再来
首周销量已经证明，这个点子能吸引足够多的人买单。
11月17日，游戏又把师生大战搬上了双层秋游大巴。新地图之外，更新加入了查询最近共同游玩玩家的功能，方便大家找到刚刚合拍的队友；房主也能设置上课铃权限，减少随意操作带来的干扰。
团队同时根据首周对局数据，调整了部分地图的阵营平衡。
对罗斯基来说，这也是《最差一届》后续值得观察的地方：一个依靠日常经验迅速被理解的游戏，怎样通过后续设计，让玩家持续制造新的故事。
校园题材的潜力，在这里得到了充分呈现。玩家买下它，是为了重新捣一次乱。顽核社则借着这间教室，找到了一条更适合自己的开发道路。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: GTA 6 changes the way you steal cars: here's everything you need to know about slim jims, key cloners, and tracking devices
author: Christopher Livingston
text:
Used to be that all you needed to steal a car in a GTA game was a few seconds and a sharp elbow. In GTA 6 , you can still smash a window and hotwire some cars, but the car stealing system has changed a lot and the further you get into the game, the more tools you'll need.
That means a quick getaway in a stolen vehicle isn't always that simple. Here are the methods for stealing cars, the new tools you'll get and when they become available in the story, and everything else you need to know about boosting rides in GTA 6.
Breaking into cars
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Want to steal a car? Walk up to the door and press the interact button. That'll tell you if it's locked (most are), if it's alarmed (nearly all are), and if it's keyless—a new type of car that we'll cover more below.
If you smash the window, you'll then climb into the car and need to hotwire it, which just takes a second or two and uses the control sticks to find the "sweet spot." If it's a keyless car, you won't be able to hotwire it or drive it away—again, more on that below. If you smash a window on an alarmed car, the alarm will sound, which can attract attention.
Carjacking
You can still pull people out of their cars, but be warned: many of them will fight back, meaning you'll need to hammer a button quickly to defeat them. Lose, and they'll clonk your head against the side of the car, knocking you down and speeding away. And even if you do pull them out of their car, this is Leonida: a lot of motorists are armed and aren't shy about opening fire.
You can't slim jim a car someone is already sitting in, so you'll have to break the window if the door is locked. Plus, there are car trackers to worry about now: more on that below.
Waink It app
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) In Chapter 1 , in the sixth story mission called Unwanted Attention , your buddy Cal will help you install the "Waink It" app on your phone, which lets you scan cars to see their make and model, if they're locked, alarmed, keyless, or have trackers. The app will also tell you the condition of the car, how much it can be sold for, and what it costs to register them—registering stolen cars at Pay 'n' Spray shops is how you take ownership of them in GTA 6.
Slim jim
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Want to get into a locked car without breaking the window or setting off the alarm? You'll need a slim jim , a tool that lets you pop the lock and open the door quietly.
You'll get this new tool in Chapter 2 of the main story, in the fifth mission called "Moses," where you meet an auto mechanic (Moses!) who will give you a slim jim and teach you how to use it. Now when you sidle up to a car door, you'll be able to use the slim jim to pop the lock: no broken windows, no alarms—though it takes a little longer than using your elbow. Again, you still won't be able to start keyless cars, even if you have a slim jim.
Keyless cars and the key cloner
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Here's the big one. Keyless cars can't be hotwired, so you'll need a key cloner . You'll get the key cloner in Chapter 3, in the 16th mission called "Steal the Zorruso for Randy." That's a long time to wait, but now you can stand next to the door of a keyless car and use your phone to clone its key.
Bonus: the key cloner will not only unlock the door but automatically start the car. That makes it worth the wait! However, keyless cars often come with another new system: trackers.
Trackers
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Standard trackers
Not a big deal, really: if a car has a standard tracker, it just means you can't modify it at a mod shop unless you've paid to register the car as your own. I probably wouldn't modify a car unless I owned it anyway, so I never worried about standard trackers at all.
Advanced trackers
These can be a problem. Advanced trackers will notify the police that the car has been stolen and pinpoint your location—and the cops will respond quickly. To defeat the advanced tracker, you need to drive fast enough that the tracker won't be able to send a signal to the cops. Slow down, and it'll start beeping and you'll only have a few seconds to speed up again. If you fail to speed up enough, the tracker will pinpoint your location and the cops will be on you again.
You have to drive pretty fast to keep the advanced tracker from triggering, which makes it tougher to get them to a Pay 'n' Spray or a Randy's garage without doing some serious damage to the car. Good luck!
Selling and storage
You can sell stolen cars at a Pay 'n' Spray, though there's a limit of three cars per day. You can also sell to your two automobile fences , Moses and Randy, though Moses only buys older model, low-end cars and Randy only buys certain flashy, expensive cars. Your Waink It app will tell you if a car is suitable for sale to either of them.
You can also store stolen cars at a garage if you've purchased one through the real estate app on your phone. Each garage only has room for a single car. You can also use a parking spot or spots outside your current safehouse to store a stolen car.

title: I finished GTA 6's main story: Ask me anything! (except for major spoilers)
author: Christopher Livingston
text:
I've been secretly playing Grand Theft Auto 6 for the past several weeks and my suffering is finally at an end.
Not that I suffered from playing GTA 6! I had a blast, actually, and as I laid out in my not-a-review this morning, I really like the game. In fact, after putting in about 100 hours, I'm ready for 100 more, though I desperately wish the game were on PC.
You know, the way it should be. The way it's meant to be.
No, my suffering is that for the past two weeks I haven't been able to talk about GTA 6 with anyone, so I'm positively bursting to let a few things fly. With that in mind, here's my invitation to you:
Ask me anything! In the comments below, ask me whatever burning questions you might have about GTA 6. I'm gonna be at my desk all day (and most of the night, probably), so I'll answer them as promptly as I can.
I don't mean ask stuff like "how does it end" or anything that could be considered a major spoiler, but stuff about how Jason and Lucia's relationship works, the activities, the characters, the world, the systems, and honestly, any other questions you might have about the game. I'll be checking the comments section for the next few days and on Friday we'll (probably) turn your questions and my answers into a story for the site.

title: WoW: Forever is huge: Players have created over 15 million characters so far
author: Tyler Colp
text:
Even though Grand Theft Auto 6 will be taking over the world tomorrow, World of Warcraft: Forever was the first game this month that people flocked to in record-breaking numbers.
While we don't know the exact player count like we do with games on Steam, we can make an educated guess on just how many people dove into the MMO via a recent set of statistics from Blizzard. According to the official WoW X account , over 15 million characters were created in the last few weeks.
Characters aren't individual players. You can create dozens of characters on your account if you want to, but I'd guess most people didn't do that. This is a game where you can put hundreds of hours into one character before ever reaching the level cap. There definitely aren't 15 million total players based on this statistic, but the number might not be massively below that.
That's a big deal for WoW, an MMO that hasn't boasted numbers like that since 2010 at the height of the Wrath of the Lich King expansion, when it had over 12 million active subscribers . Blizzard stopped posting exact numbers after that, so it's possible later expansions went higher, but it certainly seems like WoW: Forever has eclipsed the last several years of modern WoW. Blizzard even called it "the biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players," a few days after its debut.
(Image credit: Blizzard) I can't say I'm surprised that a spin-off MMO that will remain stuck in the most universally nostalgic era of WoW was a big hit. Everyone who stopped playing for one reason or another came back to remember what it was like to smack a scorpion for 38 seconds .
Whether or not they'll stick around is the question. Blizzard plans on updating the game with new things to do for players at different stages of the long leveling journey. Most people are still weeks away from reaching the level 60 cap, partially because there are so many things to do that don't involve XP. The first raid is around the corner, but I'm curious to see what kind of stuff is added for those of us who are still chilling in the mid-30s. It'd better be good because many of us will be on vacation in Leonida for the next several weeks.

title: Befuddled Japanese player fights GTA 6 controls, loses, becomes 'guy chugging two shakes I accidentally bought while walking around in a squat'
author: Lincoln Carpenter
text:
It's here. GTA 6 has been loosed upon the world, and another nation's productivity goes dark as each advancing hour unleashes midnight unlocks on the next timezone. And hey, from the sounds of it, people seem to like what they're finding —and they're finding a lot.
You can mini-golf. You can go on beach dates. You can text and drive (don't). You can doomscroll, and birdwatch, and ride a jetski with a dog . GTA 6 is dense with possible activities, actions, systems, and mechanics, but not everyone is having the best luck navigating the maelstrom of associated controls and button prompts. Allow me to present Japanese X user @Shunep3_STS , who on this day represents all of us:
操作が増えて覚えきれず、間違えて２つ買ったシェイクをしゃがみ歩きしながら飲み干すヤバい奴になってる https://t.co/OLXaEQGc7C November 18, 2026
"There are so many new controls I can’t keep them all straight," said @Shunep3_STS via machine translation, "and now I’m that guy chugging two shakes I accidentally bought while walking around in a squat."
There's something magical about this image. To begin with, the scene—like all of GTA 6—looks profoundly, almost grotesquely expensive : the delicate feathering of Jason's forearm hair, the pseudo-memoji of Cal in the text message notification, the fidelity of pebbled sand that probably cost more to realize in-game than I've spent on rent in the last three years. It's a tableau of technological excess.
And all of that's being deployed to present a man double-fisting slushies in an empty parking lot as he skulks like an imperiled raccoon. Look at him! Look at his face! He's got his chiseled jaw set like he's Solid Snake, but he's nursing a tummy full of iced corn syrup because the pilot controlling his body got too overwhelmed by which buttons do what.
(Image credit: Rockstar) And he's not alone: Our own Andrea Shearon is one of the many struggling to keep up with the sheer volume of button prompts in GTA 6. "There's so much going on," she said. "I just walk up to people and kind of mash all the face buttons for a surprise. You never know if I'm gonna punch someone or do squats or flip them off."
She's spent a lot of time accidentally making rude gestures at her snake as a result.
Amidst all the breathless praise, clips of psychopathic violence, reactionary outrage-mongering, and general noise coming out of GTA 6's launch, @Shunep3_STS's moment of shame feels very pure. It's a universal experience: No matter how much a game is hyped up, no matter how much money is spent on making it look as impressive as humanly and technologically possible, no matter how much we might want it to, we all inevitably find a way to fumble the controls so badly that the illusion entirely breaks down.
We're all, at some point, a man huddling in the dark, trying to figure out how to put down his sippy cups.

title: Rockstar says a PS5 Pro is simply 'not powerful enough' for 60 fps GTA 6, as I crack a smile at my 5090
author: Morgan Park
text:
If I can pinpoint one disappointing aspect of GTA 6 that most will agree on, it's the fact that it runs at 30 fps.
Many of us remember when this was normal for consoles (especially the PS3/Xbox 360 era), but these days, it's unusual for a major game to not offer a 60 fps or 40 fps performance option. Unfortunately, even if you're rocking a PS5 Pro, GTA 6 moves at a filmic 30.
That's disappointing news for anyone who shelled out $900+ for the more powerful PS5 Pro expecting better performance (or vindicating news, if you're a PC Gamer reader waiting for the arbitrarily delayed PC version), but Rockstar insists there was no way around it.
Speaking to Kotaku , technology production director Marc Chambers explained that the current consoles just aren't powerful enough to keep up without significant compromises.
"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," he said. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."
Head of development Rob Nelson framed the decision to skip performance mode in much simpler terms to IGN :
"It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they’re, like, ‘Have you seen it?’ There’s too many compromises that would’ve had to have been made to do that, is the short answer," he said. "Too much, too much."
While I don't actually have a problem playing a slow-paced game like GTA 6 at half the usual framerate so long as it's consistent and smooth, I can't deny that these quotes left me cracking a smile in the direction of my PC.
Rockstar Games Rockstar The world of Leonida does look unbelievably impressive at times—both in terms of pure graphical oomph and the density of vehicles, NPCs, and reactive foliage—but a great PC is going to demolish it. I've been searching for a game that will make this RTX 5090 actually flinch, and honestly, I'm doubtful even GTA 6 will be it. Barring a suite of PC-only enhancements that raise its requirements by a lot, I can't imagine a game that targets an Xbox Series S will have trouble blowing past 60 fps on top PC hardware.
This is putting into perspective for me that, while I wasn't looking, the current consoles got old. That's fine, to be clear—we're in the middle of a tech pause that has me happily playing older games anyway—but it's a wasted opportunity that GTA 6 is debuting exclusively on mid hardware.
We have to wait an unspecified amount of time to get what is destined to be the best version of this generational game. As Chris said in his writeup after 100 hours with GTA 6 , "It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC."

Barring a suite of PC-only enhancements that raise its requirements by a lot, I can't imagine a game that targets an Xbox Series S will have trouble blowing past 60 fps on top PC hardware.

This is putting into perspective for me that, while I wasn't looking, the current consoles got old. That's fine, to be clear—we're in the middle of a tech pause that has me happily playing older games anyway—but it's a wasted opportunity that GTA 6 is debuting exclusively on mid hardware.

We have to wait an unspecified amount of time to get what is destined to be the best version of this generational game. As Chris said in his writeup after 100 hours with GTA 6, "It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC."

title: Devolver's not just launching a game on the same day as GTA 6, it's using a shot-by-shot remake of the GTA 6 launch trailer too
author: Andy Chalk
text:
While most game studios are carefully avoiding the Grand Theft Auto 6 behemoth, Devolver Digital has relentlessly and theatrically pursued it. In May 2025 it pledged to launch a game on May 26, head-to-head with GTA 6—and when GTA 6 was delayed, Devolver delayed too .
And now, with GTA 6 slowly rolling through its official launch on November 19, it's finally (almost) here: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, "a spectacular remaster of the original remake of the unreleased action-platformer starring the most famous videogame mascot of all time," developed by Gunbrella/Gato Roboto studio Doinksoft.
So, first things first: As the word "unreleased" amidst that slurry of words from the Steam page suggests, this is not actually a remake of a popular game from the days of yore, although it certainly has the vibe , and actually looks pretty decent as these things go. And yes, Volvy is indeed Devolver's mascot—here's some massively overpriced merchandise , if you're into that, or just want evidence.
"Adventure across four revamped worlds full of naughty baddies and menacing boss fights while collecting delicious onions to keep Volvy at extreme levels of awesome," Devolver said of the game. "There's some sort of story too. Basically some warlocks released some slime and Volvy is stopping them. Also, they kidnapped his friends."
What really brings us here, though, is that dogged pursuit of GTA 6. It's obviously coattails marketing, but as PC Gamer's Shaun Prescott said in 2025, it's a pretty good bit—and Devolver is really sticking with it.
Yes indeed, the Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed launch trailer is a virtual shot-for-shot remake of the GTA 6 launch trailer, music and all.
Here's the GTA 6 take, so you can judge for yourself just how close it comes:
That is a pretty good bit, alright.
Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed will set you back $5 on Steam when it goes live on November 19. But the shenanigans aren't quite over yet: Devolver is also offering "a chance" at a free copy of the game to anyone who sends a video showing them deleting their GTA 6 preload, and streaming "the tunes of Devolver’s storied history" on "KVOLE Devolvy Digital radio" on YouTube . I'm listening now—it's actually pretty good.

title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 lead writer left Sandfall Interactive last summer: 'We've parted ways'
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead writer of the hit 2025 RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , has revealed that she is no longer with developer Sandfall Interactive. In an interview with Gamesbeat , Svedberg-Yen said she wants to return to her own creative efforts, including stories for film and television, and also aims to set up a new fund specifically to support the advancement of narrative design in games.
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was universally acclaimed and won an astounding list of awards, including just about every narrative-focused prize you can name: Best Storytelling at the Golden Joysticks, Best Narrative at The Game Awards, Outstanding Achievement in Story at DICE, Best Narrative at the GDC Awards, Best Narrative at the BAFTAs, and Hugo and Nebula awards. That makes it particularly interesting that Clair Obscur is Svedberg-Yen's one and only game credit: Prior to joining Sandfall Interactive in 2020 as one of its earliest members, she spent years working in the finance industry.
Despite Clair Obscur's success, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she moved on from the game, and the studio, earlier this year. "I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she said. "We’ve parted ways."
That has to hurt for Sandfall, but Svedberg-Yen still has ambitions within the game industry, including the creation of an investment fund for "narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers."
"This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face," Svedberg-Yen said. "To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.
"In that way I can also help them build a stronger narrative foundation from the beginning. I’ve done a lot of consulting work with different studios. I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations."
Svedberg-Yen said a lot of studios think of narrative as "a skin," something thrown on near the end of the development process once everything else is assembled. But that's like trying to solve a puzzle without knowing whether there's actually a solution at all, she continued, "whereas if you start from the very beginning, when everyone is starting from the same jumping-off point, everything will naturally be able to tie together."
The goal is not to compete with publishers, she explained, but "to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make."
That investment fund, alongside her own projects and stories, will be Svedberg-Yen's primary focus in the coming year: "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry."

title: GTA 6: Where to find your first plane and helicopter right away
author: Christopher Livingston
text:
If you've just started GTA 6 you might be wondering where the nearest airplane and helicopter are located to your starting point. There's a huge new world to explore, and the best way to do it is by air. But first, you've got to find a plane or chopper to steal.
Luckily, there's a reliable spot to snag your first few aircraft close to your starting safehouse, and you can probably steal them without raising a single alarm.
Where to find your first airplane
You'll drive about 2.5 miles southwest from Jason's house in Key Lento. Start the trip by driving southwest through Key Lento , then west through Abismo Key , and finally west and then north to Southwind .
You'll be taking Sunbelt Highway (Route 1) the whole way and you'll know you're close after you cross two long bridges . Southwind is a small district located next to the Mile Zero Air Station: GTA 6's military base.
(Image credit: Rockstar Games)
(Image credit: Rockstar Games)
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) (Yes, the military base has planes and helicopters too, but it's a little trickier getting your hands on them so check out our GTA 6 military base guide before you attempt it.)
The highway will make a bend to the north as you enter Southwind. On your right you'll see a concrete barrier alongside the road, and where it ends is where you want to turn right into the parking lot , at the sign for SBW (Sherwin Boatworks) and Chicki's Tiki Bar.
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) If you're facing the water (east), on your right (to the south) is a small hangar with (typically) a few Mammoth Dodo seaplanes parked inside and around it, and often a couple more moored off the dock. Seaplanes aren't the fastest planes in the game, but they're perfect for early exploration because they can land on both water and land, and they require almost no room to get airborne.
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) There's never anyone hanging around here, either, so you won't draw any attention if you help yourself to one of these planes. Just drive one into the water and take off, or steal one from the dock.
Where to find your first helicopter
Follow the same instructions to Southwind as above, but instead of looking to the south, look straight east from the entrance to the parking lot . There's an open gate leading out to a dock where a Buckingham Maverick helicopter is sitting.
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Just ignore the no trespassing sign, run over to the dock, and hop into it. Now the skies are yours.

If you're facing the water (east), on your right (to the south) is a small hangar with (typically) a few Mammoth Dodo seaplanes parked inside and around it, and often a couple more moored off the dock. Seaplanes aren't the fastest planes in the game, but they're perfect for early exploration because they can land on both water and land, and they require almost no room to get airborne.

There's never anyone hanging around here, either, so you won't draw any attention if you help yourself to one of these planes. Just drive one into the water and take off, or steal one from the dock.

Follow the same instructions to Southwind as above, but instead of looking to the south, look straight east from the entrance to the parking lot. There's an open gate leading out to a dock where a Buckingham Maverick helicopter is sitting.

Just ignore the no trespassing sign, run over to the dock, and hop into it. Now the skies are yours.

title: Set phasers to stun (the contents of my wallet): Magic's Star Trek crossover is one of the good ones
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
I recruited the biggest Star Trek fan I know to help me road test the new Magic: The Gathering set. Right away he was impressed by cards that referenced the Star Trek: Prodigy cartoon and Star Trek Beyond—a third movie in the J. J. Abrams-verse I completely forgot was even made—but if that kind of trainspotting was all it took to make a successful crossover then people would have liked the Spider-Man cards a lot more than they did.
What makes the better Universes Beyond crossovers work is how they bring out the themes of their source material, turning motifs into mechanics that make a set feel like a genuine expression of the thing being adapted rather than just another property being fed into the content machine. Having played some games with the cards, yeah, I think Star Trek works.
I built a blue-green deck around Strange New Worlds , a mechanic that rewards you for having different lands rather than just stacking Islands and Forests. When I played Deep Space Scan I drew a card for each differently named land I had, and those lands also lowered the cost of powering up my Astute Terraformer.
Meanwhile, the Federation mechanic gives bonuses for having different creature types on the table like Vulcan and Klingon and Romulan (though not Borg). With just those two mechanics, the set emphasizes exploration and diversity. You really do want to put together a crew representing multiple species and send them into the final frontier. (There is of course a card called Final Frontier.)
Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Wizards of the Coast Star Trek also makes use of the spacecraft mechanics introduced in Edge of Eternities, where a ship starts with limited capabilities but has to be stationed by tapping creatures to add charge counters to access its full abilities—like flying and fighting. Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge is a solid combo, doubling the amount of charge counters you add each time and letting you get the Enterprise into the air twice as fast.
There are cards for various different iterations of the Enterprise, but I'm partial to U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit, because when you play it you get three red 1/1 officer tokens for free. That makes it faster to station, and after that you've got three disposable officers to chump block with. Which is why they're red .
There's also a Beam Me Up mechanic to bring a card back from the discard pile at the cost of returning a card from the table to your hand, and a cute assimilate mechanic that lets you wipe creatures' existing types then turn them into artifacts under your control for your Borg deck. But what makes the Star Trek cards feel like Star Trek is how much they emphasize teamwork.
The Common Goal card lets two creatures deal damage together, and there's a whole suite of cards that get better when you've got creatures with a total power of 8 attacking as one. Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior, who doubles his own power when he's part of that attack, proved a gamewinner for my red/white deck more than once. The thing that really comes across is Star Trek's utopian ideal of everyone pulling together in a crisis and being better for our differences. It's optimistic, with stars in its eyes, and even a casual Star Trek watcher like me can appreciate that.
Magic: The Gathering's Star Trek set is available now, for both tabletop Magic and Arena.

title: Over an hour of new Total War: Warhammer 40,000 campaign footage shows gear customization, fleet mechanics, and emphasizes space marines are not always trusted and hard to replace
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
The last time we got a decent look at Total War: Warhammer 40,000 was the Gamescom build, which Fraser Brown called the highlight of his year . Since then Creative Assembly has continued iterating and a more recent build was subject to a friends-and-family playtest, then shown off in an "alpha strike" livestream that lasted a solid hour and 20 minutes.
Beginning 23 turns into an Ultramarines campaign, we got to see the battle for the Praevoss system, which has three conquerable planets in it—as well as a gas giant and a dead world that can't be fought over.
Each system in Total War: Warhammer 40,000 gets a separate narrative, a mini-campaign that plays out before you move on to the next system, taking some but not all of what you've built with you. That seems like an interesting way of dealing with the grand strategy problem of campaigns getting boring when you've painted half the map, but still have 100 turns before the end. Having a soft reset and facing different foes in a different theatre would keep a campaign feeling fresh.
In the Praevoss system the Ultramarines' objective is to liberate Imperial planets from an ork scourge. When the marines take a region, one of the options they have is to "scour the battlefield" in return for a big payout in Requisition, at the cost of raised Suspicion. Calling down a fleet bombardment to soften up orks ahead of the battle also raises Suspicion because there are still civilians in the area. Oops.
It's an interesting part of the fiction to emulate: Imperial planets having their own governments and maybe resenting the transhuman giants who've been sent to liberate them. Space marines have gone rogue before—the head of the Astral Claws chapter infamously hoarded planetary tithes for himself and became known as the Tyrant of Badab, and of course there's the whole Horus Heresy thing—and a random Imperial governor might not be thrilled at the angels of death stomping across their world.
Playing nice prevents Suspicion from going up and rewards the marines with Influence points, which they spend to gain reinforcements from local Imperial troopers. That seems super useful because of another way Total War: Warhammer 40,000 emulates the fiction, which is making space marines difficult to replace.
Where other factions replenish losses after battles, the marines are much more limited. It takes a decade to train each one after all, and there are only so many progenoid glands to go around. The livestream shows that while some casualties return after battle thanks to their transhuman physiology letting them survive injuries that would normally be fatal—and as we've already seen, important characters who fall can be jammed into dreadnoughts —actual reinforcements have to be called down from the orbiting fleet. They can even arrive mid-battle via drop pods that slam down right on top of the enemy.
The Total War: Warhammer trilogy is all about making each faction play differently, and I'm glad to see that carry over even to the vanilla Ultramarines. The customization options, which let you outfit them with bespoke wargear loadouts, speak to a similar dedication to detail.
What's missing from the livestream is any suggestion of fleet battles in Total War: Warhammer 40,000. The ships in orbit seem to play an important part in the campaign, but as a source of reinforcements and bombardments and a way of moving armies between planets. I guess if we want to play 40K ship battles Battlefleet Gothic: Armada 2 already exists and is quite good.

The last time we got a decent look at Total War: Warhammer 40,000 was the Gamescom build, which Fraser Brown called the highlight of his year. Since then Creative Assembly has continued iterating and a more recent build was subject to a friends-and-family playtest, then shown off in an "alpha strike" livestream that lasted a solid hour and 20 minutes.

Beginning 23 turns into an Ultramarines campaign, we got to see the battle for the Praevoss system, which has three conquerable planets in it—as well as a gas giant and a dead world that can't be fought over.

Each system in Total War: Warhammer 40,000 gets a separate narrative, a mini-campaign that plays out before you move on to the next system, taking some but not all of what you've built with you. That seems like an interesting way of dealing with the grand strategy problem of campaigns getting boring when you've painted half the map, but still have 100 turns before the end. Having a soft reset and facing different foes in a different theatre would keep a campaign feeling fresh.

In the Praevoss system the Ultramarines' objective is to liberate Imperial planets from an ork scourge. When the marines take a region, one of the options they have is to "scour the battlefield" in return for a big payout in Requisition, at the cost of raised Suspicion. Calling down a fleet bombardment to soften up orks ahead of the battle also raises Suspicion because there are still civilians in the area. Oops.

It's an interesting part of the fiction to emulate: Imperial planets having their own governments and maybe resenting the transhuman giants who've been sent to liberate them. Space marines have gone rogue before—the head of the Astral Claws chapter infamously hoarded planetary tithes for himself and became known as the Tyrant of Badab, and of course there's the whole Horus Heresy thing—and a random Imperial governor might not be thrilled at the angels of death stomping across their world.

Playing nice prevents Suspicion from going up and rewards the marines with Influence points, which they spend to gain reinforcements from local Imperial troopers. That seems super useful because of another way Total War: Warhammer 40,000 emulates the fiction, which is making space marines difficult to replace.

Where other factions replenish losses after battles, the marines are much more limited. It takes a decade to train each one after all, and there are only so many progenoid glands to go around. The livestream shows that while some casualties return after battle thanks to their transhuman physiology letting them survive injuries that would normally be fatal—and as we've already seen, important characters who fall can be jammed into dreadnoughts—actual reinforcements have to be called down from the orbiting fleet. They can even arrive mid-battle via drop pods that slam down right on top of the enemy.

The Total War: Warhammer trilogy is all about making each faction play differently, and I'm glad to see that carry over even to the vanilla Ultramarines. The customization options, which let you outfit them with bespoke wargear loadouts, speak to a similar dedication to detail.

What's missing from the livestream is any suggestion of fleet battles in Total War: Warhammer 40,000. The ships in orbit seem to play an important part in the campaign, but as a source of reinforcements and bombardments and a way of moving armies between planets. I guess if we want to play 40K ship battles Battlefleet Gothic: Armada 2 already exists and is quite good.

title: Not even Walton Goggins knows if Fallout will have a Season 4: 'if we get the opportunity to come back for season four, that would continue to honor how sacred this is to people'
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
I'm psyched for Fallout's third season whenever it comes out (Kyle MacLachlan says it could be May or June next year ), but I'd be perfectly happy if it had an ending and the show was done. Better to tell your story and leave it there than drag out a show just because it's popular and end up finishing on a wet fart of a finale when you should have gone out on, er, whatever the opposite of a wet fart is.
Season 3 has finished filming, but right now not even Walton Goggins, who plays The Ghoul, is sure what the future holds for Fallout's TV incarnation. Talking about how the show's maintaining the "subversive humor and the satirical kind of elements" it brought over from the games at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar , he said, "I feel confident that we've done that in season three, and if we get the opportunity to come back for season four, that would continue to honor how sacred this is to people. It's not something that we take lightly."
Goggins as we know doesn't play videogames himself. And co-star Aaron Moten has sworn off playing Fallout , leaving Ella Purnell the only actor to roll a Vault Dweller out of the headline trio. But despite that, Goggins is still aware of what the games mean to people.
"I mean, my son is a gamer. I see exactly how and why he plays games. I'm not a gamer at all, but the game of Fallout has been around for such a long time. It's been a shared experience between parents and their children and friends for such a long time, but it holds a very special place in their heart," Goggins said.
"I think what they have responded to, at least what I've been told out on the road, is the reverence in which all of us approach the sacred nature of this game, and while still keeping it an original story in the canon of Fallout."
Fallout Season 3 will feature another definite videogame-enjoyer in its cast, though. Aaron Paul, star of Dispatch and some other stuff I guess, has joined the show 16 years after attending a launch event for Fallout: New Vegas .

title: Bank your cash in GTA 6, but always keep a few hundred on you—you never know when you'll need it
author: Sean Martin
text:
Cash is king in GTA 6 , and Rockstar has come up with some new systems to manage your finances, from a secret stash under the floorboards to an honest-to-goodness interest-bearing savings account.
But you need to be careful with your money, especially at the start of the game when even a few hundred bucks can make or break you. While wandering around Leonida, strangers might try to rob you (big mistake), but more importantly, if you die or get arrested, you'll be penalized a few hundred dollars. There's also a $20k limit to how much you can keep on your person as you gradually accumulate more and more through play.
The solution? Stash your cash frequently. During the initial chapters of the game, you won't have a bank account, but you can store your money in your house in Key Lento by simply stashing it under the floorboards in the bedroom. This will mean you have a little money tucked away, and won't lose it when you die or get busted by the cops. .
Remember, you can also stash stolen goods like jewelry, drugs, and marked bills from robberies in the trunk of your car. Even if your car gets impounded by the fuzz, you'll be able to recover that contraband from your trunk later on and sell it. Don't stash goods in a car you don't own, though: you might lose it if you lose that car.
The stash in Jason's house is a great way to store money before you unlock banking (Image credit: Rockstar) Here's the important bit of advice: you might be tempted to deposit all your cash, but if you do, you'll miss out on a variety of real-time and random opportunities in the game. There are a bunch of street encounters in GTA 6 reliant on you having some cash in your pocket, such as the time a stranger promised to tell me a secret in exchange for a few dollars—and then offered me more secrets for even more money, and then teased me with the biggest secret of all for more cash than I had on me. I'm still wondering what that final secret was!
Sometimes you'll have the opportunity to bribe someone for quick access to a restricted area, or you'll meet a pool hustler in a dive bar and want to pony up cash for a quick game. GTA 6's living city and its random occurrences are part of the attraction of the game, after all. There are a few vendors that only take cash, too. The point is, when you're making your deposits, always hold back a few hundred for your wallet.
When you reach the mission called "Buck Me" in Chapter 1 you'll unlock a bank account, which will more easily let you deposit your cash in nearby ATMs. You can spot these on the map by the hand with the credit card symbol—just walk up to one and interact with it to dump your cash. Having an account will also unlock certain weapons for purchase.
The Buck Me app on your phone also lets you "Buck Yourself"—transfer money into a joint savings account Jason and Lucia share. Any money you put into that savings account can't be withdrawn, so while it's good to sock away funds for the future, keep in mind you're shutting yourself off from your own money.
No matter how responsible (or irresponsible) you are with your cashflow, always remember to keep a few hundred in your wallet. If one of GTA 6's cash-based encounters happens, the last thing you want to do is have to run off and look for the nearest ATM.

title: Refueling cars in GTA 6 is barely necessary, but there's much better reason to visit garages
author: Sean Martin
text:
Having to refuel cars in GTA 6 was weirdly one of the most talked about features before launch—I guess people didn't like the idea of having to pull over for gas while being chased by half the Vice City's police department. But the reality is that refuelling cars is something you'll barely find yourself doing.
When your ride does run low on fuel, you can find a gas station on the map via the gas pump symbols:
Pull up to a pump close enough to see the prompt for "Services"
Select "Refuel" (It will also display the $ cost)
Press the interact button
You'll see Jason or Lucia picking up the pump handle
Hold down the button shown in the lower right corner to refuel
When you're done, you'll see Jason or Lucia replace the pump handle
You'll be back in your car
Easy, right? And you'll barely have to do it since, just like real life, cars can go quite a long time without refuelling if they have a full tank, even if you're going over 60mph, which I assume you are. Note that if you steal a stranger's car, their tank may nearly be empty already.
If you're driving an electric car, check the map for recharging stations. Pull up close to one, select "Charge Vehicle," and it'll display the cost. You'll see a quick scene of the readout on the charging station filling the battery to 100%, and when it's done, you can drive away.
(Image credit: Rockstar) Now, the better reason to visit Vice City's fuel stations is that they can repair your vehicle, and if you drive like I do, you'll need this a lot. This is a separate interaction at the same gas pump: on the"Services" menu, just select "Repair" instead. The camera will whoosh into the sky for a moment, and when it returns to ground level your ride will be fixed.
The cost depends on how much damage you've done to your vehicle, but it's well worth it if you want to retain your ride, considering the usual vehicular wear-and-tear that comes with being a professional criminal.
Since you can customise your beloved vehicles at the Mod Shop, or even claim fancier cars by removing their trackers at the Pay 'n' Spray, once you unlock this in the story, keeping your car in good condition is a worthwhile investment.

title: Looking for free guns and body armor in GTA 6? Try the trunks of cop cars
author: Sean Martin
text:
Remember how stealing a cop car in the older GTA games used to get you a free shotgun? Well, turns out Vice City's police force is even better armed. If you need some extra guns quickly, particularly shotguns and assault rifles, filching them from the trunk of a police car is a great method, though obviously it comes with certain risks.
You might have realised, but stealing cars in GTA 6 is significantly more complicated than previous games, especially if they're alarmed. Thankfully, this doesn't apply to any police pickup trucks like the Bravado Bison the cops sometimes use, which you'll spot occasionally both in rural areas and in the city
With the police pickups, you can simply climb onto the bed at the back and open the storage crate, grabbing any weapons and ammo inside, including other potential items like Stun Guns, without setting off any alarms.
For proper police cruisers, though, their trunks are alarmed along with the doors, meaning you'll need a tool to deal with them, the slim jim , which you get during the "Moses" mission in Chapter 2. If you slim jim the door of the cop car and get inside, the trunk will unlock, so you can head around the back, interact to open it, and steal whatever's in the boot without tackling the alarm, whether it be an assault rifle, shotgun, or even body armor.
The best way to open the boot is to break into the car itself Rockstar This unlocks the boot, which often contains assault rifles, shotguns, or body armor Rockstar If you don't have the slim jim yet, you can still open the trunk (you'll see your character use a screwdriver) but the alarm will go off.
Once you've collected the weapons, you can interact with your own car trunk, and you'll see a prompt to stow the weapons inside. You'll be rather conspicuous wandering around with an assault rifle in your hands or strapped to your back, after all.
Obviously, it's best not to try and steal cop cars with cops in them , but you can find them around, or parked at police stations, such as in Port Gellhorn or Vice City.
More generally, it's definitely worth looting random car trunks to see what you can find. Sometimes they contain cash, drugs, handguns, or consumables—just make sure to scan them with the Wainkit App first (which you're introduced to in Chapter 1) to tell if they're alarmed or not, and whether you can break in without the slim jim.

title: Former Rockstar president's studio is looking to sue its way out of a £61 million debt, and yes, it's still claiming MindsEye suffered 'a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews'
author: Harvey Randall
text:
The saga of MindsEye has been somewhat concerning to watch from a distance. Originally pretty interesting, given it was headed up by former Rockstar North president Leslie Benzies, it instead became a poorly-received videogame (this is me being polite ). One which would be a shame under any other circumstances, but has since spun out into a trainwreck saga involving multiple layoffs and, most notably, a lot of finger-pointing at alleged "saboteurs" .
Many of its actual developers happen to disagree , a whopping 93 of them alleging "systemic mistreatment, mismanagement, and mishandling of the redundancy process" back in October of last year. The studio itself has continued to try and update it , including with a mission that is about those alleged saboteurs , which is a normal thing you do when you are trying to be taken seriously.
Anyway, the layoffs are continuing , and it looks like it's sink or swim for Build a Rocket Boy. Things have never gotten sinkier or swimmier than right now, however, as both a statement of affairs and a notice of administrator's proposal filed November 16 (and unlocked yesterday) have painted a picture , as spotted by RedbullCola on ResetEra .
It's bad. The picture's looking bad.
Build a Rocket Boy has an unsecured creditor claim—that is to say, debt—of around £61 million: "Unsecured creditor claims are presently estimated at approximately £61.752 million, principally comprising amounts due to group undertakings, Diameter, NetEase and various trade creditors."
Unsurprisingly, Build a Rocket Boy is still hooked on the saboteurs thing: "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary. The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties."
The plan? Sue the pants off everybody. "The Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals. The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration."
It's that last bit: "Largest asset". When your largest asset is the hypothetical money that'll come from the pendulum of justice finally swinging your way, you're in deep trouble. And given how little concrete evidence has emerged so far of a wider conspiracy against a game we gave an honest shot and just found to be plain bad? I do not think this is going to work.

title: DDR6 memory modules to be almost half the size of DDR5 and almost double the max speed
author: James Bentley
text:
You may not be able to buy memory right now, but the good news for a hopeful future is there's potentially quicker and smaller RAM on the horizon. JEDEC, the council that sets industry standards for RAM, has published a preview of what DDR6 could look like, and it seems like it will be itty and bitty.
According to JEDEC, DDR6 will bring with it higher bandwidth, higher capacities, better reliability, more energy efficiency, and different form factors (via VideoCardz ).
Starting with bandwidth, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at a speed of 12.8 GT/s and are set to move up to "14.4 GT/s and beyond." DDR5 maxes out at 9.2 GT/s, representing a sizable bump. It also expands the data bus from 64 to 96 DQ, which no doubt contributes to the bandwidth increase.
That is fast, though not two times faster like DDR5 versus DDR4. It is worth noting, however, that memory modules tend to get faster over their lifetime so we don't know where that might end up.
The module for DDR6 is now 74 mm, which is almost half of the 133 mm for DDR5. This is supposedly "intended to help accommodate higher system memory density", with DDR6 supporting up to 128 GB DRAM die density (double that of DDR5).
There are other gains to be had with DDR6 too. JEDEC says it targets an improved performance-per-watt over DDR5 "through a change to VSS-terminated IO and data-center-focused low power modes"
JEDEC says DDR6 can support a "breadth of form factors", including RDIMM, UDIMM, CAMM.
Now for one thing you may not want to hear, but might have already suspected: JEDEC says DDR6 is 'built for the data center". It says its interface is "optimised for high-capacity modules with configurations oriented to general purpose compute as well as AI inferencing and agentic AI, which demand more capacity and performance close to the CPU."
(Image credit: Remitski via Getty Images) Being built for data center usage does not mean consumers will be left out in the cold, of course, but it does further signal just how much memory is being designed for future AI usage. And the memory crisis seems set to last at least through 2027, even if Acer's CEO reckons it's impossible for it to last until 2030 . It is all heavily reliant on how much memory supply can be ramped up and how much memory demand comes from the AI boom, which is certainly a hard-to-predict industry.
Continuing the trend of news you don't want to hear, we don't know when DDR6 is supposed to be available to the public. It seems like the release window is between 2028 and 2029, but we don't have any more information than that. And that's before musing on whether we non-AI data center owners will ever be able to afford the module. Hopefully, the memory crisis will cool off in a couple of years, and DDR6 will actually be affordable for PC gamers, though whether it will be relevant for PC gaming is a whole other thing. But, to steal a line from The Shawshank Redemption, "Hope is a dangerous thing".
